items.title: You can’t collect 13th month salary and vote against APC, Oborevwori tells Delta workers
items.description: By Egufe Yafugborhi & Ochuko Akuopha ASABA – DELTA State Governor, Sheriff Oborevwori, has declared that no civil servant in the state will vote against the All Progressives Congress, APC, in the 2027 polls because of his administration’s 13th month salary package. Oborevwori spoke on Thursday in Asaba during the inauguration of the Delta State APC Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, where he unveiled “MORE Plus” as theme of his re-election campaign. The governor, who is chairman of the council, said the 13th month salary has tied the fate of workers to the continuity of his administration. “Today civil servants have no choice not to vote us. They have no choice. 13th month (salary) is huge, times two. Some people don’t understand what 13th month,” Oborevwori said. He explained: “What you’re receiving now is times two in December. That is the meaning of 13th month. Whether you’re an appointee, whether a public servant, whether a civil servant, you’re receiving your 13th month.” Oborevwori charged members of the council to take President Bola Tinubu’s message to the grassroots and mobilise voters across units and wards. He described membership of the council as a call to service, urging members to work with unity, discipline and dedication to secure victory for President Tinubu, himself and other APC candidates. “Our achievements must speak for us, but we must also be prepared to explain them convincingly,” he said, urging members to communicate the impact of government policies and his M.O.R.E Agenda focusing on infrastructure, education, healthcare, workers’ welfare, youth empowerment and security. Deputy Governor, Sir Monday Onyeme, commended Oborevwori for aligning Delta with the Federal Government, urging party faithful to consolidate the gains. Onyeme said: “We must publicise Tinubu’s achievements in areas such as local government autonomy, education funding, grassroots development, security, electricity and road infrastructure.” Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, defended Tinubu’s economic reforms. Keyamo argued that difficult decisions were necessary to address the country’s economic challenges, saying the reforms had caused temporary hardship but were intended to address underlying problems, including the unsustainable cost of fuel subsidies. Delta APC Chairman, Chief Solomon Arenyeka, said the inauguration demonstrated the party’s readiness to contest and win elections at all levels in 2027. Former Governor, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa, who spoke for Delta North, said expectations were high following the state’s mass defection from PDP to APC in April 2025. Okowa urged the council to demonstrate strength through impressive electoral performance, stressing the need to reach voters directly rather than rely solely on rallies. Speaking for Delta Central, Olorogun O’tega Emerhor expressed delight that APC is now the ruling party in Delta, pledging support for re-election of Tinubu and Oborevwori. For Delta South, former Secretary to State Government, Comrade Ovuozourie Macaulay, said the Oborevwori administration’s achievements would help the campaign, assuring that the district would work towards delivering substantial votes. Director-General of the campaign council, Senator James Manager, pledged to work with party leaders and members to secure victory for the APC, describing the assignment as an onerous task requiring collective effort and sustained grassroots mobilisation. The post You can’t collect 13th month salary and vote against APC, Oborevwori tells Delta workers appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Senate advances research and innovation fund bill
items.description: — Proposal earmarks 20% of Nigerian Content Development Fund for research By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Senate has passed for second reading a bill seeking to establish the National Research and Innovation Development Fund and the National Council on Research and Innovation to strengthen research funding and the commercialisation of research outcomes in Nigeria. The proposed legislation seeks to create a sustainable institutional and financial framework for coordinating, funding and supporting research, development and innovation across relevant sectors of the economy. Sponsored by the Senate Leader, Senator Opeyemi Bamidele (APC, Ekiti Central), the executive bill is titled National Research and Innovation Development Fund and National Council on Research and Innovation (Establishment) Bill, 2026 (SB. 1069). Following its second reading, the bill was referred to the Senate Committee on Tertiary Institutions and TETFund for further legislative action. Leading the debate on the bill’s general principles, the Senate Chief Whip, Senator Tahir Monguno (APC, Borno North), said research and innovation were critical to Nigeria’s economic competitiveness and national development. Monguno noted that Nigeria had universities, polytechnics, research institutes, professional academies and technology entrepreneurs engaged in research and development, but argued that their potential could be better harnessed through coordinated activities, sustainable funding and stronger collaboration. He said the proposed fund would support indigenous and emerging technologies, research infrastructure, projects addressing Nigeria’s specific challenges and a national database of research, development and innovation resources and outputs. The bill also seeks to strengthen collaboration among government, academia, industry and communities to ensure that research findings are translated into commercially viable products, services and practical solutions. On funding, Monguno said Section 19 of the bill proposed that the fund’s resources should include an annual contribution equivalent to 20 per cent of the Nigerian Content Development Fund, appropriations by the National Assembly, grants, donations, endowments, proceeds from patents and commercialisation, investment income and other lawful sources. He said Section 20 outlined the proposed uses of the fund, including research grants, innovation initiatives, infrastructure, product development and prototyping, indigenous technology development, intellectual property acquisition, technology transfer, capacity building and commercialisation of research outcomes. According to Monguno, Section 21 proposes limiting administrative expenditure to no more than 25 per cent of the annual contribution from the Nigerian Content Development Fund. He said the provision was intended to ensure that a greater proportion of the designated funding went towards research and innovation activities rather than administration. The proposed legislation also contains accountability provisions covering annual estimates, financial records, audits, annual reports and oversight by the National Council and a proposed Joint Ministerial Committee responsible for budget approvals. It further outlines offences and penalties relating to the alleged diversion or misapplication of grants, failure to account for funds, submission of false information, unauthorised disclosure of information, obstruction of officials and conflicts of interest. On intellectual property, Monguno said the bill proposed a framework for determining ownership of intellectual property arising from funded research, protecting the interests of researchers and beneficiary institutions, and facilitating technology transfer and commercialisation. He said the fund could help develop local solutions in agriculture, healthcare, education, manufacturing and environmental management, while creating opportunities for young Nigerians and encouraging private-sector participation and contributions from Nigerians in the diaspora. Monguno, however, stressed the need for clear priorities, rigorous assessment of research proposals, measurable outcomes and effective monitoring of funded projects if the legislation became law. He said the proposed fund should serve as a credible national mechanism for supporting research excellence, encouraging innovation and ensuring that funded projects delivered tangible benefits to the economy and society. The post Senate advances research and innovation fund bill appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: PM vows to bring back progress to KP, assails PTI's 'callousness' during its tenures
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday vowed that the federal government, which now runs Khyber Pakhtunkhwa under governor’s rule, would make every effort possible to “bring back” progress to the province. He made the remarks while chairing a meeting of the apex committee in Peshawar, where he arrived earlier in the day on his first visit to the province since the imposition of governor’s rule and the declaration of emergency on Oct 11. The meeting, attended by Chief of Defence Forces and Chief of Army Staff Field Marshal Asim Munir and KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi, reviewed KP’s overall security situation. Federal ministers and newly appointed provincial advisers were also present. Addressing the committee, PM Shehbaz reiterated that emergency and governor’s rule had to be imposed “under extreme compulsion”. “I promise that we will leave no stone unturned in bringing back the happiness and era of progress to this province, and in the practical realisation of the wishes, aspirations, and dreams of this province’s people that have been shattered due to the worst actions of recent years,” he said. The prime minister affirmed that the Centre “will place all possible resources at your feet”. He added that himself, the Advisory Council led by the governor, the president and the CDF “will ensure that this province, once again, not only matches the other provinces in the race for development, but I would be extremely happy if it moves even further ahead”. The prime minister regretted that “terrorists were summoned back here” after peace had been established, “washing down all sacrifices down the drain”. “There can be no greater enmity with the country than not honouring and respecting such sacrifices, not holding them in esteem,” he remarked, highlighting that young soldiers left their homes and families to defend their country. The premier called for an “all-encompassing analysis as to why this happened”, adding that there was “no worse callousness, criminal negligence, and hostility towards the national interest than this”. He said: “All issues of the people were pushed aside — whether it is education, healthcare, or protecting the lives and property of the people — and [having] matters with terrorists instead. I believe that no other example can be found of such hostility against the country, in terms of their attitudes, detachment, and callousness.” PM Shehbaz asserted that 5,000 police vacancies were not filled, Safe City projects were yet to be completed, the capacity of the Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) had not been enhanced significantly, and neither were special measures taken regarding police training. He recalled that all provinces had agreed at the time of the 2010 National Finance Commission Award that KP, being the front-line region in combatting terrorism, needed ample resources. “From 2010 to today, more than Rs800 billion in funds have either already been provided or are being provided under this,” he stressed. “However, not only did it resurface, but the weapons needed to counter terrorism, the required capacity, and the trained officers needed were nowhere to be found.” While saying he would not go into the details, the prime minister emphasised that he had assured the provincial governments of ex-chief ministers Ali Amin Gandapur and Sohail Afridi of the Centre’s full support in the fight against terrorism. “But nothing was done regarding this,” he regretted, adding that the government could not remain a “silent spectator” when a “party was stooping to such enmity against the country” and the economy and society were being destroyed. “Therefore, on this occasion we made this one last effort,” the premier said, referring to the province’s interim handover to the federal government under governor’s rule. Highlighting the Centre’s efforts to stabilise the economy over the past two and a half years, PM Shehbaz remarked, “It wouldn’t have been possible [without] unprecedented partnership between political and military hierarchy.” He said the federal government could not remain a silent spectator when “terrorists were roaming around dancing in all areas of KP, and were ruling over some areas in the evening, and collecting extortion” at a time when the stabilisation of Pakistan’s economy was being acknowledged globally. The prime minister recalled the breakdown of the Oct 3 talks between the Centre and reiterated that his government was “compelled to make this decision” of imposing governor’s rule. PM Shehbaz remarked that the province was “shattered with wounds due to the circumstances created in the past several years”. He highlighted the poor law and order situation over the past six years, recalling that security forces and law enforcement agencies had made sacrifices to establish peace in KP. The premier said there was corruption of Rs100bn in the clean drinking water of the Cities Improvement Project and Rs37bn in the “infamous looting” in the case of the Kohistan District Accounts Office . He said that “80,000 people were martyred and the [economy] suffered a loss of several hundred billion dollars. Only then, in 2018, was peace completely restored in this country”. Describing the province as “very beautiful”, the premier expressed his hope that the government “work hard day and night and speedily make it progress towards development and prosperity”. “This is the province that is the first extremely strong wall of the homeland,” he noted. Centre announces Rs160bn uplift funds, other measures PM Shehbaz later also attended a meeting of the Area Representative and Development Council (ARDC) constituted for 12 districts of KP, which face serious security challenges. CDF Munir was also present on the occasion. The council covers Dera Ismail Khan, Tank, Lakki Marwat, Bannu, Bajaur, Mohmand, Khyber, Kurram, Orakzai, North Waziristan, South Waziristan Upper and South Waziristan Lower. It includes 48 elders and prominent personalities from those districts to ensure local representation. Addressing the ARDC, the prime minister announced that the federal government would provide KP with Rs160bn for development projects. Furthermore, to address the wheat shortage in the province, he said the Centre would provide KP “as much wheat as is needed” from the storages of Pakistan Agricultural Storage and Services Corporation (Passco). “However, there should be no hoarding. And whatever price the Centre provides wheat at, the common man should get wheat at that very price,” the premier emphasised. He went on to assure the ARDC that the federal government will provide “whatever assistance” in operations and resources is needed to fight terrorism. He also said directives have been issued to bolster the CTD and complete Safe City projects. PM Shehbaz also asserted that any difficulties in the completion of the federal government’s projects in KP will be resolved, adding that the governor-led administration will address problems in provincial projects. The prime minister appreciated the tribal elders for always supporting Pakistan unequivocally and said the ARDC now had an “immense responsibility”. Noting the remarks of ARDC Chairman Shaukatullah Khan, PM Shehbaz said: “He stated that development work is zero, corruption is 100 per cent, and terrorism is at its peak. I completely agree with him.” The premier referred to weaknesses in the police’s performance, stating that arrests in cases of theft and robbery were not made. Mentioning examples of corruption, such as the Kohistan scandal, he said: “You will feel great pain and sorrow over how the province’s resources were looted. God willing, this will be fully controlled, and every single penny of your development and prosperity will be delivered to your doorstep.” Police’s vehicle procurement ban relaxed: Kundi Separately, in a bid to improve the police’s capabilities amid the current law and order situation in the province, Kundi said he has approved the relaxation of the police’s vehicle procurement ban to ensure personnel have the necessary resources. In a post on X, Kundi said that in line with the prevailing security landscape in the province, he approved the relaxation of the ban. “Our [KP police] force stands on the front lines to protect the lives and security of our people,” he wrote. “In the prevailing law and order situation, ensuring that our officers have the vehicles and resources they need is essential to an effective response to security challenges.” Kundi added that the restrictions would be loosened “within the approved scope and against funds already allocated in the Police Procurement Plan”. “This will strengthen operational capacity without placing any additional burden on the provincial exchequer,” he noted. “Supporting our police is not just a responsibility; it is an investment in the safety of our people and the peace of KP.” In July this year, the KP government had imposed a ban on the procurement of vehicles except for ambulances; earth-moving machinery; fire trucks; tractors; trucks; buses; passenger vans; prisoner vans; motorcycles; water tankers; rescue and recovery vehicles and boats; and mobile laboratory vehicles, according to an order issued by the KP finance department. “In case of [an] essential requirement, the chief minister, Khyber Pakhtunkhwa, may relax the ban on [a] case-to-case basis,” the order, seen by Dawn , read. Development of merged districts a ‘special priority’ In his address to the apex committee, the KP governor termed establishing peace and stability in KP a “collective priority”, and stressed that it was in the interests of the entire country. Referring to the federal government’s decision to impose emergency and governor’s rule in KP, Kundi said that the peaceful transition showed that the people of the province wanted peace and stability. “I want to pay tribute to my people who showed restraint despite the turmoil,” he said, asserting there had been no untoward incident in the region following the measures. On Oct 14, three days after emergency was imposed, a protest demonstration by PTI workers in Khyber’s Bara tehsil turned violent as protesters clashed with police. Injuries to party workers and cops were reported in the incident. Speaking at the meeting, Kundi also paid tribute to those who sacrificed their lives in the war against terrorism, including personnel of the police, army, Frontier Corps, and Federal Constabulary. “These sacrifices demand a more effective strategy to combat terrorism,” he underscored. The governor reiterated that the foremost priority of his KP Advisory Council was to restore peace and eliminate terrorism. Kundi termed the development of the merged districts a “special priority”. “The people of these regions have paid a heavy price during this fight against terrorism. Now, they deserve better education, health, and economic opportunities,” he declared. “The federal government’s cooperation in establishing peace and stability in the province is very significant,” the PPP leader highlighted, saying he was keen to play his role in this collective endeavour. The governor maintained that the people of KP would not have to choose between peace and development. “This is our collective responsibility to provide people with both.” Kundi declared that the KP Advisory Council would keep playing its role in integrating these merged areas in the circle of national development. “The public’s trust is the only metric of measuring our success in the war on terror,” he asserted, while reaffirming that the whole network of terrorism would be annihilated, and the facilitators and financiers of terrorists would also be targeted. “I seek constant support and supervision by the federal government,” he asked, expressing the hope that the Centre would continue its cooperation. Emergency amid security challenges The Centre had imposed emergency and governor’s rule in KP on Oct 11, citing the PTI-led provincial government’s “deliberate disengagement” from the fight against terrorism. The decisions were also endorsed by the Parliament last week amid protests by the opposition. Governor Kundi, along with Interior Minister Mohsin Naqvi, had chaired a meeting of the provincial apex committee a day after governor’s rule was imposed. In the meeting, the governor — who is now in charge of running the province — assured Naqvi he would enforce all policies of the federal government and work together with the security forces for peace and prosperity of the province. Kundi asserted that under the new set-up, tackling terrorism would be the priority. Later that day, Kundi, addressing a press conference, called for greater coordination between the Centre and the province, stressing that policies on counterterrorism will “come from Islamabad [..] not Kabul,” in an apparent jibe at the PTI-led KP government, which has been accused of maintaining a “nexus” with terrorist groups by federal ministers. The Centre’s move to impose governor’s rule and emergency in KP also followed a mobilisation drive and protest march by the PTI and in opposition at the Centre, to demand the release of its jailed founder, Imran Khan. Intense negotiations between the two sides a week before the imposition of governor’s rule had failed to yield any results, with counterterrorism policy being one of the main reasons behind the breakdown of their talks. The PTI said it was being left out of security decisions concerning KP, which the Centre denied . It also called for reviewing the counterterrorism policy, while the latter criticised the KP government’s efforts to combat terrorism in the province and objected to its stance on dialogue with the Afghan Taliban. Soon after, the Centre also authorised the deployment of Pakistan Army troops and assets in aid of civil power in KP. Federal ministers have also alleged that the PTI-led government in KP had a “nexus” with terrorist groups, stating that the province’s security situation necessitated the imposition of emergency there. Additional input by Irfan Raza

items.title: ‘You have another son in me,’ Obi tells slain supporter’s mother
items.description: — NDC candidate pledges continued support to bereaved family By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The presidential candidate of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), Peter Obi, has pledged continued support to the family of Ifeanyi Nwolie, his supporter who was shot dead during a political activity in Enugu State. Obi gave the assurance on Thursday while attending Nwolie’s burial in his hometown of Afa, Udi Local Government Area of Enugu State, telling the deceased’s mother that she had gained another son in him. According to reports from the event, Obi also pledged to continue the monthly financial support Nwolie had been providing for his mother and sent the family an amount covering 15 months, through December 2027. Nwolie was among supporters who participated in an NDC political activity on October 10, 2026, which was marred by violence. He was shot dead during the incident. In a post on his X handle, Obi said he arrived at the Nnamdi Azikiwe International Airport, Abuja, from the United Kingdom at 5:30 a.m. on Thursday before connecting to a 7 a.m. flight to Enugu to attend the burial. He described Nwolie’s death as a painful reminder of the human cost of political violence in the country. “My humble pledge to the mother is that God Almighty, whom it pleased to bring Ifeanyi home, has also given her another son in me to support her, as Ifeanyi used to,” Obi said. As the country prepares for the 2027 general elections, the former Anambra State governor called on candidates at the federal, state and local government levels to reject violence, ethnic division and religious bigotry. He urged political parties and candidates to focus their campaigns on issues capable of improving the country, stressing that citizens must be able to express their political choices and participate in the electoral process without fear. “The process through which we attain public office is more important than the office itself,” he said. Obi also emphasised the importance of the rule of law, warning that undermining it could lead to disorder and anarchy. He called for collective efforts to build a country where human life is valued above political ambition and citizens can exercise their democratic rights in peace and safety. “A new Nigeria is possible,” he said. The post ‘You have another son in me,’ Obi tells slain supporter’s mother appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Atiku raises alarm over ‘missing’ voters’ register, demands INEC action
items.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA — Former Vice President Atiku Abubakar has raised the alarm over the alleged failure of the Independent National Electoral Commission, INEC, to publish the preliminary voters’ register for public scrutiny, warning that the lapse could undermine confidence in the 2027 general election. Atiku said Nigerians could not verify the commission’s claim that more than 103 million voters had been registered when the register was reportedly unavailable on its online portal during the October 9 to 15 inspection period. In a statement on Thursday by Phrank Shaibu, Director of Strategic Communication of the African Democratic Congress, ADC, Presidential Campaign Council, Atiku demanded the immediate publication of the register, questioning conflicting accounts of when it was displayed and raising concerns about safeguards against electoral fraud. “INEC has announced more than 103 million registered voters. Nigerians went to its portal to inspect the names and found an empty page. That is an outrage. A figure cannot answer an objection. A press announcement cannot tell a voter whether her name has been omitted. Show Nigerians the register,” he said. Atiku also questioned reports that INEC’s chairman had said on October 5 that the public display had already been completed, despite the commission’s subsequent announcement of an October 9 to 15 inspection period. “Which statement is true? Where was the register published? For seven full days, or for no days at all? INEC must produce the dates, the links and the records of access,” he demanded. The former vice president further raised concerns over Section 63(2) of the Electoral Act 2026, which permits a returning officer to count a ballot paper without INEC’s official mark if satisfied that it came from a book supplied to the polling unit. He argued that the provision required enforceable safeguards to establish the origin of such ballot papers and prevent counterfeit votes. “Nigerians cannot be denied access to the voters’ register before election day and then be asked to accept unmarked ballot papers after voting. INEC must set out enforceable safeguards against counterfeit ballots, and the National Assembly must close any loophole that leaves the authenticity of a vote to an officer’s unsupported assurance,” Atiku said. The ADC campaign council also faulted INEC for failing to respond to inquiries about the identities of companies awarded contracts to print sensitive election materials, raising a separate question about transparency in the handling of critical electoral materials. Taking the dispute directly to President Bola Tinubu, Atiku linked the controversy to the economic hardship and insecurity facing Nigerians, warning against asking voters to trust an election process they could not scrutinise. “You will not add an unseen voters’ register to their suffering and call it a route to another four years in office,” he said. Atiku warned that denying voters access to the register would leave them unable to establish who had been added, whose name had been removed or whether their own details remained intact. He said the ADC would challenge any denial of voters’ rights through lawful means. He called on INEC to publish the register by local government, area council and ward, explain the conflicting dates and give voters the opportunity to challenge false entries and correct omissions. The former vice president also urged Nigeria’s international partners, election observers and democratic institutions to press the commission to comply with the law before election day. “Do not wait until election day to ask whether this contest is credible. Demand access to the voters’ register now. Ask how every ballot paper will be authenticated. Transparency before the vote is as essential as scrutiny of the results afterward,” he said. The post 2027: Atiku raises alarm over ‘missing’ voters’ register, demands INEC action appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: 2027: Ex-deputy governors seek credible leaders
items.description: — Forum calls for security investment, ex-convicts’ reintegration — Demands merit-based recruitment, women’s inclusion and stronger grassroots engagement By Henry Umoru ABUJA — The Forum of Former Deputy Governors of Nigeria (FFDG-N) has called for a reassessment of the country’s leadership recruitment process ahead of the 2027 general elections to ensure the emergence of credible individuals capable of earning citizens’ trust. The forum also urged the Federal Government to sustain investment in security agencies, establish effective reintegration programmes for ex-convicts and strengthen grassroots engagement between political representatives and citizens. The demands were contained in a communiqué issued on Thursday at the end of the forum’s fifth National Conference, held from October 20 to 21 at the Abuja Continental Hotel, Abuja. The conference was themed, “Rethinking Nation-Building: Bridging the Leadership-Citizen Disconnect Through Orientation, Attitude, Character, Culture and Tradition Towards Sustainable Development.” The event was chaired by former Katsina State Governor, Aminu Bello Masari, and co-chaired by former Delta State Governor, Senator Ifeanyi Okowa. According to the communiqué, Nigeria’s democracy can thrive when the leadership recruitment process produces credible individuals who command public confidence and possess the legitimacy to lead. “Recruitment processes into the public service of Nigeria should accord considerable attention to competence and character in ways that selection systems prioritise merit,” the forum said. It also called for the reassessment of political leadership selection, while urging political leaders to support young Nigerians to pursue digital innovation and creativity. On security, the forum commended the Federal Government and security agencies for their efforts to secure the country, urging continued investment in the agencies to improve their operational efficiency. It further called on the government to establish effective programmes for reintegrating former inmates into society. “The Federal Government should institute an effective programme for reintegration of ex-convicts in society,” the communiqué stated. The forum also urged the government to harness Nigeria’s youthful population, agricultural potential, solid mineral resources and intellectual and technological capacity to promote national development. It specifically called for the completion of the Ajaokuta Steel Complex as part of efforts to advance nation-building and sustainable development. On governance and public service delivery, the former deputy governors called for the full implementation of service standards specifying expected processing times, communication requirements, accessibility provisions and mechanisms for complaints and feedback. They also urged the Federal Government to develop a strategic communication framework requiring public officials to communicate openly and honestly about government achievements and challenges. The forum said such a framework would help reduce public suspicion surrounding governance. It further called for an effective regulatory framework for the use of artificial intelligence in the country. On inclusion, the forum advocated governance structures that would guarantee greater representation for women, young people and marginalised minorities. It recommended the institutionalisation of gender quotas for executive positions and legislative seats at the federal, state and local government levels. The communiqué also urged the government to define the constitutional role of traditional rulers more clearly to strengthen their contributions to cultural preservation and modern governance. It called on governments at all levels to preserve and adapt enduring cultural values to promote ethical leadership, social cohesion and national development. The forum further advocated stronger family and community values, mutual respect between leaders and citizens, and the formalisation of consultative assemblies at ward levels to improve regular communication between elected representatives and communities. It also called for vigorous public enlightenment on Chapter Two of the 1999 Constitution, as amended, particularly its Fundamental Objectives and Directive Principles of State Policy, as a means of promoting patriotism. The forum added that teachers’ remuneration should be improved to strengthen their capacity to serve as role models. The communiqué was signed by the forum’s National Chairman, Dr Chris Alomash; Deputy National Chairman, South, Hazeem Gbolarumi; and Deputy National Chairman, North, Muktar Ahmed Anka. The post 2027: Ex-deputy governors seek credible leaders appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Damang Gold Mine can operate for 15 more years with the right investment – Engineer
items.description: Mechanical engineer and certified inspecting engineer Obed Asamoah has expressed confidence in the future of Damang Gold Mine, saying the mine could remain operational for at least 15 more years if it receives the necessary investment. Speaking at a special edition of Asempa FM’s Ekosiisen programme in Tarkwa on Thursday, October 22, he argued that the transition to a new investor should not be viewed as a fundamental change to the mine’s operations. Mr Asamoah said the previous operator was primarily an investor, suggesting that the key requirement for sustaining the mine was adequate capital to support its operations and development. “I realised that the previous operator was only an investor, so the only thing that has changed is the investor. All we need is the money to invest,” he said. Based on his assessment, he maintained that Damang had considerable operational potential and could remain productive well beyond the next decade, provided the necessary resources were available. “I can boldly tell you today that, based on my own limited findings, Damang Gold Mine can continue operating for the next 15 years and beyond. The mine has a future, so we should be confident,” he added. Mr Asamoah also reflected on his initial reservations about the ability of a Ghanaian operator to manage the mine, saying his experience had changed his perspective. He urged others not to hold onto his earlier doubts, arguing that local professionals were capable of managing major industrial operations. “Do not follow my initial position of not believing in a Ghanaian operator. When I joined, I realised that the black man is capable of managing his own affairs,” he said. The Damang Mine, formerly operated by Gold Fields Ghana Limited, was officially handed over to Engineers and Planners in April 2026, following the company’s successful bid for the concession. The handover ceremony took place at the mine site on Saturday, April 18, 2026, where the Minister for Lands and Natural Resources, Emmanuel Armah-Kofi Buah, performed the symbolic transfer. This was after Gold Fields’ lease expired, and the government placed the concession under competitive tender supervised by the Minerals Commission.

items.title: 4 cops including DSP martyred, 2 terrorists killed during exchange of fire in KP's Karak: police
items.description: LAKKI MARWAT: Four policemen, including two officials, were martyred and two terrorists were killed during an exchange of fire in Khyber Pakhtunkhwa’s Karak district on Thursday, police said. A statement by the KP police said law enforcers had initiated a search and strike operation in the Charpara area at noon, where terrorists had set up a blockade on Wednesday night. Banda Daud Shah and Counter-Terrorism Department (CTD) deputy superintendents of police (DSP) led the operation, in which bomb disposal unit (BDU) personnel, a drone team, Rescue 15 personnel and Rapid Response Force personnel also participated, the statement said. “During the operation, the law enforcers raided the hideout of a terrorist commander, Qaiser Iqbal, where an exchange of fire took place,” the police said, adding that two terrorists were killed in the encounter. CTD DSP Imranuddin Khan, Latambar Station House Officer (SHO) Sub-Inspector (SI) Afzal Awan, Constable Kazim and Head Constable Amjad from the BDU were martyred in the exchange of fire. The statement said the operation was ongoing. It added, “The brave martyred personnel of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa Police have set a shining example of dedication to duty, courage, and a commitment to public safety by sacrificing their lives in the fight against terrorism.” The statement said the sacrifices of the martyred policemen reflected the police force’s “unwavering resolve” to continue making every possible effort to eradicate terrorism and establish lasting peace in the region. KP Governor Faisal Karim Kundi condemned the incident and expressed sorrow over the martyrdom of four police personnel. “The sacrifices of the Khyber Pakhtunkhwa police in the fight against terrorism are unforgettable. The blood of our martyrs will not go to waste; our resolve against terrorism will be further strengthened, and the struggle for the establishment of peace will continue,” he said. KP has been witnessing terrorist attacks and security challenges for a long time, including attacks on police personnel. Thursday’s operation comes around 20 days after several terrorist hideouts were destroyed during a joint search and strike operation in Karak. In September, two terrorists were killed in an intelligence-based operation in Lakki Marwat, and in August, a police constable was martyred and six officials were injured when an improvised explosive device was used to attack a police patrol van. According to a recent report from the Centre for Research and Security Studies, Pakistan recor­ded a sharp 83 per cent increase in violence-linked fatalities during the third quarter of 2026, re­­versing a declining trend reported in the first and second quarters as terrorism and counter-terrorism deaths surged nationwide. Balochistan and KP remained the epicentres of violence, jointly accounting for 98pc of all fatalities during the period. Balochistan recorded 829 deaths, nearly 59pc of the national total, while KP reported 556 fatalities, accounting for more than 39pc.

items.title: Programme gouvernemental : l'Alliance de la gauche annonce son vote contre
items.description: Lors de la discussion du programme gouvernemental, jeudi 22 octobre à la Chambre des représentants, Nabila Jalal, députée de l'Alliance de la gauche, a dénoncé le manque d’engagements chiffrés de la nouvelle équipe. Emploi, pouvoir d’achat, services publics, fiscalité et lutte contre la corruption : l’élue a décliné cinq critères à l’aune desquels elle entend juger l’action du gouvernement, avant d’annoncer que son groupe voterait contre le programme. La promesse d’un « changement de cap » ne convainc pas Nabila Jalal. Pour la députée de l'Alliance de la gauche, le programme gouvernemental 2026-2031 ne rompt pas suffisamment avec les pratiques de l’exécutif précédent et reste en deçà des attentes sociales. Jeudi 22 octobre, lors de la discussion du programme à la Chambre des représentants, elle a livré une intervention à charge contre la nouvelle majorité, mettant en cause la crédibilité de ses engagements et l’absence, selon elle, de garanties concrètes pour les mettre en œuvre. D’emblée, l’élue a rappelé la participation de l’actuelle cheffe du gouvernement aux décisions de la précédente équipe, qu’elle accuse d’avoir favorisé « l’alliance flagrante entre l’argent et le pouvoir « , les conflits d’intérêts et les intérêts des lobbies des hydrocarbures. Elle lui reproche également d’avoir contribué à l’appauvrissement de la classe moyenne et des travailleurs, tandis que le capital rentier bénéficiait, selon elle, d’un traitement privilégié. Pour étayer ses critiques, Nabila Jalal a évoqué la saisie de bulletins de vote à Tanger et les suspicions de fraude électorale qui s'en sont suivis, ainsi que la révocation d’une ministre quarante-huit heures après sa nomination, estimant que cet épisode révèle des défaillances dans le choix des responsables et soulève des interrogations sur la capacité de l’exécutif à contrôler des marchés publics de plusieurs milliards de dirhams. Au-delà de ces accusations, la députée a placé le débat sur le terrain de la responsabilité politique. Elle a notamment dénoncé l’absence, dans la déclaration gouvernementale, de mesures qu’elle juge indispensables à une réforme institutionnelle, plaidant notamment pour la reddition des comptes. Cinq critères pour juger le gouvernement Le cœur de son intervention repose sur cinq épreuves censées mesurer la capacité du programme à répondre aux préoccupations des Marocains. La première concerne l’emploi. Nabila Jalal a rappelé que les partis de la majorité avaient promis la création d’un million de postes et une réduction du taux de chômage à 7 % à l’horizon 2031. Elle déplore que la déclaration gouvernementale ne précise ni le nombre d’emplois à créer ni un objectif chiffré de baisse du chômage. Elle regrette également l’absence de référence au salaire minimum, jugeant insuffisante la mise en avant de la formation et de l’expérience professionnelle : « La formation n’est pas un emploi, et l’expérience professionnelle ne constitue pas un contrat de travail », a-t-elle lancé. Le deuxième test porte sur le pouvoir d’achat. L’élue critique le recul, selon elle, de plusieurs promesses électorales. La gratuité automatique et sans conditions de la facture d’électricité aurait ainsi été remplacée par un dispositif d’aide destiné aux ménages considérés comme éligibles. Elle dénonce également le report à une mise en œuvre progressive de l’exonération fiscale des salaires inférieurs à 15.000 dirhams et de la promesse d’une pension de retraite d’au moins 3.000 dirhams. La question du salaire minimum décent, annoncé par un parti allié pour 2027, aurait, elle aussi, été repoussée à la fin du mandat. Sur les hydrocarbures, Nabila Jalal regrette l’absence d’engagement concernant le plafonnement des prix et la remise en service de la raffinerie Samir. Elle estime que les intérêts des détenteurs de monopoles demeurent insuffisamment encadrés. Troisième priorité : la santé et l’éducation. La députée dénonce la dégradation des services publics, le déficit de ressources humaines et le poids du secteur privé, auquel elle attribue 91 % des dépenses de l’assurance-maladie. Elle s’interroge sur les garanties apportées par le programme en matière de gratuité des soins, d’accès à l’enseignement et à l’université, d’augmentation des bourses étudiantes et de financement de la recherche scientifique. Le quatrième critère concerne la justice fiscale. Nabila Jalal met en doute le financement des ambitions économiques affichées par la majorité. Elle relève que son parti mise sur la mobilisation de 300 milliards de dirhams, sur une enveloppe globale de 350 milliards, grâce aux effets additionnels de la croissance. Elle confronte ces projections aux objectifs annoncés par le gouvernement : une croissance de 5 %, un déficit budgétaire inférieur à 3 % et un endettement inférieur à 62 %. La députée reproche surtout à la nouvelle équipe d’avoir relégué au second plan les promesses de taxation des revenus de la rente, des grandes fortunes et des bénéfices issus des monopoles. Elle voit dans les références à l’élargissement de l’assiette fiscale et à la restructuration du portefeuille public le risque d’une nouvelle vague de privatisations. À ses yeux, la protection sociale doit plutôt reposer sur une fiscalité progressive sur la fortune, l’imposition des grands exploitants agricoles et la lutte contre la fraude fiscale. Enfin, le cinquième test porte sur la reddition des comptes. Si le gouvernement affirme que sa responsabilité sera mesurée aux résultats, demande Nabila Jalal, encore faut-il préciser les échéances et les indicateurs permettant de les évaluer. Elle pointe également les contradictions qu’elle perçoit entre la promesse de criminaliser l’enrichissement illicite et la position du ministre de la Justice, issu du parti de la cheffe du gouvernement, qui estime cette mesure contraire à la présomption d’innocence. Des revendications institutionnelles et sociales La critique du programme s’accompagne d’une série de revendications politiques. Sur les libertés publiques, Nabila Jalal a annoncé que son groupe présenterait, pour la troisième fois, une proposition d’amnistie générale en faveur des détenus du Hirak du Rif, des jeunes du mouvement « Génération Z » et des détenus politiques, journalistes, blogueurs, syndicalistes et défenseurs des droits humains. Elle réclame également l’arrêt des poursuites qu’elle qualifie d’abusives et la réparation des préjudices subis. Sur le plan territorial, elle a réaffirmé la revendication de récupération de Sebta et Melilla, des îles et des autres territoires occupés, tout en demandant un programme d’urgence pour les régions frontalières. Elle a plaidé pour que le Parlement et les forces politiques soient associés au débat sur la mise en œuvre du plan d’autonomie. Elle a également défendu une intégration effective de l’amazigh dans les politiques publiques, ainsiqu'une représentation institutionnelle des Marocains du monde. La députée a enfin mis en avant les enjeux de souveraineté hydrique et énergétique, dénonçant l’épuisement des nappes phréatiques par les cultures d’exportation subventionnées et réclamant la remise en service de la raffinerie Samir. Son programme, intitulé « La dignité d’abord », prévoit aussi une réforme de la loi sur la profession d’avocat, une meilleure prise en compte des droits des personnes en situation de handicap, une réforme équitable des retraites et une égalité effective entre les femmes et les hommes dans les postes de décision. Au terme de son intervention, Nabila Jalal a estimé que la déclaration gouvernementale ne répondait à aucune des cinq épreuves qu’elle avait définies. En conséquence, elle a annoncé que son groupe parlementaire voterait contre le programme gouvernemental, tout en promettant d’exercer pleinement ses prérogatives de contrôle et de défendre les propositions de l'Alliance de la gauche. « La dignité des Marocains est une priorité », a-t-elle conclu. items.title: FIFA okays Normalisation Committee to run Nigerian football
items.description: The Bureau of the FIFA Council on Thursday approved the appointment of a Normalisation Committee to manage the affairs of the Nigeria Football Federation, pending fresh elections into the NFF Executive Committee. According to a letter signed by FIFA Secretary General, Mattias Grafström and addressed to Dr Emmanuel Ikpeme MON, “the normalisation committee shall consist of a suitable number of members, who will be appointed jointly by FIFA and CAF as soon as possible.” The letter also informed that “the period during which the normalisation committee shall perform its functions shall expire as soon as it has fulfilled all of its tasks, but by no later than 31 May 2027.” None of the members of the normalisation committee will be eligible for the positions to be filled during the upcoming NFF elections under any circumstances. In the meantime, the Secretariat of the NFF will continue with the day-to-day running of the organisation and administration of the country’s football pending the appointment of the Normalisation Committee. items.title: Missions diplomatiques et Postes consulaires du Burkina Faso : le Camarade Karamoko Jean Marie TRAORE invite les chefs de poste à renforcer la communication pour éviter les dysfonctionnements
items.description: Le Camarade ministre des Affaires étrangères, accompagné de ses proches collaborateurs, en l’occurrence ceux de l’Inspection générale des services, a présidé un webinaire avec les chefs des Missions diplomatiques et Postes consulaires, sur la gestion budgétaire au niveau des ambassades et consulats généraux du Burkina Faso à l’étranger. Cette rencontre tenue le 21 octobre au ministère des Affaires étrangères, a également connu la participation en présentiel ou en ligne, des représentants de l’ASCE-LC, de l’inspection générale des Finances, de l’inspection technique du Trésor, de l’Agent judiciaires de l’Etat, de la Direction générale des Affaires immobilières et de l'Equipement de l'Etat (DGAIE) et de la Caisse nationale de Sécurité sociale, qui interviennent également à des niveaux différents dans le contrôle ou l’appui au fonctionnement de nos MDPC. Deuxième du genre, elle traduit la volonté du département des Affaires étrangères de renforcer la qualité de la gouvernance diplomatique, dans un contexte où la rationalisation des ressources de l’État, la transparence et l’obligation de rendre compte constituent des exigences fondamentales de l’action administrative. Il s’agit à travers cette démarche, de réduire les dysfonctionnements constatés dans la gestion administrative, des ressources humaines, du matériel mobilier et immobilier, de la commande publique et le pilotage opérationnel des activités au niveau de nos ambassades et consulats généraux. Ce cadre est initié à la suite de missions d’audit et d’appui-conseil effectuées par les corps de contrôle dans les MDPC et qui ont décelé des insuffisances récurrentes, liées non seulement au non-respect des normes de gestion administrative, comptable et financière, mais aussi à l’interprétation subjective ou parfois erronée de certains textes, qui peuvent impacter négativement le bon fonctionnement de ces MDPC. Pendant trois heures d’échanges entre premiers responsables du ministère des Affaires étrangères, chefs de MDPC et cadres du ministère de l’Economie et des Finances, il est ressorti la nécessité de mettre l’accent sur la communication, si l’on veut mettre fin aux dysfonctionnements et améliorer durablement la performance des MDPC. « Ces dysfonctionnements sont plus liés à un manque de communication ; il faut améliorer la communication au sein de nos Missions diplomatiques, entre les Missions diplomatiques et la Centrale et entre le ministère des Affaires étrangères et les autres départements, notamment celui des Finances », a insisté le Camarade Karamoko Jean Marie TARORE. Une formation du personnel diplomatique sur la gestion budgétaire s’avère également une nécessité selon la délégation du ministère en charge des Finances, afin d’éviter les manquements qui sont fréquemment décelés. A cela s’ajoute la digitalisation des services dans les MDPC qui permettra de garantir la transparence dans leur fonctionnement. Il en est de même pour l’immatriculation du personnel diplomatique pour mettre fin aux difficultés de gestion de la pension des retraités issus des MDPC, selon le représentant de la CNSS. Sur ce point, le Camarade ministre TARORE a indiqué la nécessité d’envisager une session spéciale avec la CNSS. Appelant à la rigueur et à la discipline dans l’utilisation des biens de l’Etats dans les MDPC, le ministre et les autres intervenants ont encouragé les chefs de postes, à poursuivre les efforts dans le domaine de la Comptabilité Matière, et à d'envisager l’acquisition des biens immobiliers, et ainsi amener l’Etat à quitter le statut de locataire vers celui de propriétaire. Aux chefs des MDPC qui ont salué la tenue de cette séance, le premier responsable du ministère des Affaires étrangères a demandé de prendre en compte les observations, les orientations et les recommandations formulées pour une gouvernance diplomatique dans le respect de la réglementation en vigueur au Burkina Faso. DCRP/MAE

items.title: Wike: FCT residents won’t repeat 2023 mistake, will back Tinubu in 2027
items.description: By Omeiza Ajayi ABUJA: Minister of the Federal Capital Territory FCT, Nyesom Wike, has assured President Bola Tinubu that residents of the territory will not repeat the mistake of 2023 but would back his re-election in 2027. “The mistake we made in 2023, would we make that mistake again? If it was an error, would we make that error again?” he asked a gathering in Bwari Area Council on Thursday. The audience answered no. He spoke at an interactive session of the Rainbow Coalition, a political arrangement between members of the All Progressives Congress APC, the Peoples Democratic Party PDP and some other opposition parties. Wike cautioned residents against “political gamblers” and pointed to ongoing projects in the territory as the reason to stay with the Tinubu administration. On the senator representing the FCT, Ireti Kingibe, Wike asked whether anyone had felt her presence. “Today, the people of FCT, do you feel the impact? Do you feel the presence of the senator representing FCT today?” he asked. In her place, he presented Senator Philip Aduda and John Gbadaya as the coalition’s choices. “After all, party is a vehicle that conveys you to where you are going. When you get there, you come down from the vehicle and you now work for the interest of the people,” he said. The minister revealed that the coalition’s arrangement had already cost one politician a ticket. Julius Adamu, the PDP chairmanship candidate in the last Area Council elections, stepped down for the Bwari Area Council Chairman, Joshua. Wike said he would recommend Adamu for a position in the FCT Universal Basic Education Commission. The FCT APC Chairman, Tanko Yamawo, described how deep the divide between the parties once ran. He said a former PDP chairman once refused a ride in his car for fear that sitting in an APC member’s vehicle could cost him his position. The FCT PDP Chairman, Ismaila Dogara, said the coalition “had come to stay” and that his members were ready to work for Tinubu. items.title: Aéroport international de Ouagadougou : La SAFA renforce la préparation aux situations d’urgence
items.description: La Société des Aéroports du Faso (SAFA) a tenu, ce jeudi 22 octobre 2026, une session de formation et de sensibilisation sur le Plan d’urgence d’aéroport (PUA) de l’Aéroport international de Ouagadougou. Cette initiative s’inscrit dans le cadre de la relecture et de l’actualisation de ce dispositif destiné à renforcer la préparation et la réponse aux situations d’urgence aéroportuaire. La session vise à permettre aux acteurs internes de la SAFA et aux différentes parties prenantes intervenant sur la plateforme aéroportuaire de mieux connaître leurs rôles et responsabilités, de maîtriser les procédures d’alerte et de communication et de renforcer la coordination dans la gestion des situations d’urgence. Selon Wendmanegdzanga Jean Bernard Kalmogo, directeur de la sécurité, de la qualité et de l’environnement de la SAFA, cette rencontre porte sur le Plan d’urgence d’aéroport de Ouagadougou. Soulignant le caractère obligatoire de ce dispositif, il a indiqué que « l’aéroport de Ouagadougou se conforme à la réglementation ». « Nous avons un expert qui a sensibilisé tous les acteurs qui interagissent sur la plateforme aéroportuaire sur la nécessité et l’obligation d’un plan d’urgence qui est une façon de prévenir tout risque d’incident ou d’accident. Chaque acteur a un rôle précis à jouer dans ce plan d’urgence et tout se résume à la sécurité des biens et des personnes », a-t-il expliqué. « C’est vraiment très capital pour nous parce qu’il s’agit de faire des simulations », Didier Kaboré La formation sera complétée par un exercice de sécurité sur table destiné à tester les mécanismes prévus par le PUA. Il permettra notamment d’identifier les éventuelles insuffisances liées à la chaîne d’alerte, à la prise de décision, à la coordination, à la communication, à la mobilisation des ressources et à la continuité des activités. Du côté des participants, la tenue de cette session est saluée. Pour Didier Kaboré, chef de l’unité Sauvetage et lutte contre l’incendie de l’ASECNA, le Plan d’urgence d’aéroport constitue un outil essentiel de gestion de crise. Il estime qu’il est important que tous les acteurs intervenant sur la plateforme aéroportuaire se l’approprient. « C’est vraiment très capital pour nous parce qu’il s’agit de faire des simulations », a-t-il souligné. Une appréciation partagée par Kiswendsida Catherine Compaoré, cheffe du service Réglementation et conformité de la SAFA. Selon elle, cet atelier s’inscrit dans la volonté du Burkina Faso de se conformer aux normes internationales en matière de sécurité aéroportuaire. « Cette formation est là pour nous rappeler tous les fondamentaux liés au processus de certification et notamment dans son Plan d’urgence d’aéroport », a-t-elle fait savoir. À travers cette initiative, la SAFA entend renforcer les capacités de préparation et de riposte de ses équipes et des parties prenantes externes face aux situations d’urgence. L’objectif est également de favoriser une meilleure appropriation du PUA par les décideurs et les responsables opérationnels, afin d’en faire un véritable outil d’intervention et de coordination en cas de crise. Faso7 L’article Aéroport international de Ouagadougou : La SAFA renforce la préparation aux situations d’urgence est apparu en premier sur Faso7 .

items.title: Cape Coast has more to offer tourists beyond its castles – Ridge Royal MD
items.description: The Managing Director of Ridge Royal Hotel in Cape Coast, Sheila Adjetey-Anum, says the Central Region has more tourism opportunities to offer visitors beyond its historic castles and forts. She said the region could attract more tourists, particularly members of the African diaspora, by promoting its cultural heritage, local cuisine and other attractions as part of a comprehensive tourism experience. Speaking to Myjoyonline.com on the sidelines of the ongoing 6th iNTTA Expo at Ridge Royal Hotel in Cape Coast on Thursday, October 22, she said the hospitality industry must work closely with tourism operators to package and market the region’s attractions. “We have Cape Coast Castle, we have Elmina Castle, we have Hanskate, we have quite a number of places. I mean, there’s a canopy walk that you can do, but are we selling that enough in terms of tourism?” she asked. Ms Adjetey-Anum said Ridge Royal Hotel offers packages that allow guests to explore Cape Coast and other attractions, arguing that hospitality should extend beyond providing accommodation. “When you live or stay with us at Ridge Royal, we do have packages. So we’ll let you tour Cape Coast and a few other places and all of that; so it becomes an experience,” she said. She also identified local cuisine as an area with significant potential to strengthen the region’s appeal, particularly among diaspora visitors seeking to reconnect with their heritage. “But the food, I don’t think we have given out a lot in terms of what you can get here in Cape Coast,” she said, calling for greater promotion of traditional dishes such as Fante fante, kenkey and fish. Ms Adjetey-Anum said promoting these experiences alongside the region’s historical attractions could help deepen visitors’ understanding of Ghanaian culture and encourage more people to explore Cape Coast. Her comments come as tourism and hospitality stakeholders meet at the iNTTA Expo in Cape Coast to discuss investment opportunities and strategies for growing the sector. The expo’s second day, Thursday, October 22, is being held under the theme “From Vision to Transactions”, with discussions focusing on investment opportunities across tourism, hospitality and related industries.

items.title: Atwima Mponua records 139 new HIV infections, second highest in Ashanti Region
items.description: The Atwima Mponua District has recorded 139 new HIV infections, making it the second-highest in the Ashanti Region after the Kumasi Metropolitan Assembly. The figure, according to 2025 data, was revealed at the inauguration of a nine-member District Committee of the Ghana AIDS Commission. The statistics have prompted a renewed call for urgent and coordinated action to curb the spread of the virus in the district. District Chief Executive Ibrahim Issahak, who chairs the newly inaugurated committee, is leading efforts to strengthen public education, prevention, and support services. Speaking at the ceremony, he described the situation as alarming and said the district could not afford to be complacent. He urged members of the committee to develop and implement effective, evidence-based interventions to reduce new infections. Mr. Issahak called for intensified public education, voluntary counselling and testing, an end to stigma and discrimination against persons living with HIV, and improved access to prevention, treatment, and care services. He further charged members to discharge their duties with dedication, compassion, and a strong sense of responsibility, noting that success would require sustained collaboration among health professionals, traditional authorities, religious leaders, civil society organisations, and other stakeholders. The nine-member committee comprises the DCE as Chairman; Deborah Mawuena Gaze; Margaret Nambu, representing the Ghana Education Service; Joyce Bannerman, Public Health Nurse representing the Health Directorate; Nana Amoako Ogyampa, representing the Traditional Authority; Catchiest Collins Opoku Boah, Chairman of the Local Council of Churches; David Baggania, representing Civil Society; Abu Adam, representing the Muslim community; and Ernest Kofi Ashie as focal person. The inauguration marks a major step towards a stronger district-wide response to HIV and AIDS, with the committee expected to coordinate targeted interventions and deepen community engagement. For Atwima Mponua, stakeholders agree that the fight against HIV and AIDS requires collective responsibility, consistent education, and accessible health services to protect lives.

items.title: Les Français cherchent à se procurer des armes d’autodéfense, en amont d’un nouveau week-end de mobilisation
items.description: Les recherches Google pour des mots-clefs liés à l’autodéfense, comme « achat d’armes », « armurerie », « lacrymogène » ou « batte de baseball », ont bondi à partir du 17 octobre, week-end qui a vu plus de 1 500 commerces être pris pour cible et pillés ou dégradés en marge des manifestations. À Paris, 451 commerces ont été vandalisés, dont 228 pillés et 223 dégradés, en particulier dans le Xe arrondissement, selon des chiffres de la mairie et de la préfecture de police 451 commerces vandalisés » : la carte des établissements parisiens pillés et dégradés les 17 et 18 octobre », Le Parisien , 22 octobre 2026.'> 1 . L’ampleur de la mobilisation et le nombre d’émeutiers, qui avaient été sous-estimés par le ministère de l’Intérieur, l’ont conduit à déployer un nombre insuffisant de forces de l’ordre, a reconnu Laurent Nuñez, évoquant un « manque d’anticipation ». La hausse du nombre de recherches sur Google associées à l’achat ou à la recherche d’informations sur des armes d’autodéfense ne traduit pas nécessairement un volume important de recherches. Les données Google étant relatives, elles reflètent surtout une nette hausse de l’intérêt par rapport à un niveau d’ordinaire bas, notamment pour les armes à feu, dont la détention par les civils est très encadrée en France et autorisée essentiellement dans le cadre de la chasse ou d’une pratique sportive. Elle peut également traduire le sentiment d’un État perçu comme incapable d’assurer la sécurité. En amont de nouvelles manifestations prévues samedi 24 octobre, le préfet de police, Patrice Faure, a appelé mercredi 21 octobre les commerçants à « renforcer leur sécurité » Le préfet de police de Paris conseille aux commerçants de « renforcer leur sécurité » et « d'adapter leurs horaires » avant les prochaines manifestations », Franceinfo , 22 octobre 2026.'> 2 . Celui-ci a notamment recommandé aux commerçants situés sur ou à proximité du parcours des manifestations de recourir, « s’ils le peuvent, à la sécurité privée », accompagnée le cas échéant d’équipes cynophiles, et de vérifier leurs systèmes d’alarme et de vidéoprotection. Un important dispositif sera déployé à l’échelle nationale samedi 24 octobre, avec notamment des véhicules blindés de la gendarmerie et des unités d’élite de police et de gendarmerie, tandis que des militaires de l’opération Sentinelle seront chargés de sécuriser des sites sensibles. Au total, les forces de l’ordre seront environ 20 % plus nombreuses que lors du samedi 17 octobre. items.title: « Le Soleil » et la commune de Djinaky signent un partenariat
items.description: Dans sa dynamique de vulgarisation des richesses des territoires, le quotidien national « Le Soleil » a signé, hier, mercredi 21 octobre, une convention de partenariat avec la commune de Djinaky, dans le département de Bignona. Les deux parties s'engagent à faire du développement territorial une priorité partagée. Le magazine « Soleil du Sud », édité pour le Pôle Casamance (Ziguinchor, Sédhiou, Kolda) par le média national sera le support pour cette entente. Le quotidien national « Le Soleil » et la commune de Djinaky, dans le département de Bignona, ont signé, hier, mercredi 21 octobre, une convention de partenariat. Cette collaboration vise à jeter les bases d’une nouvelle politique axée sur la vulgarisation et la promotion des potentialités des communes du Sénégal. Le directeur général du « Soleil », Lamine Niang, a magnifié cette collaboration qui, d’après lui, permettra « d’accompagner la commune de Djinaky pour faire connaître ses projets à impact réel sur sa population ». Il a, en outre, rappelé que la collectivité territoriale de Djinaky est la première institution municipale avec laquelle « Le Soleil » a signé une collaboration pour le compte du magazine « Soleil du Sud ». Il estime que ce partenariat va constituer le point de départ d’une entente qui, dans le long terme, « débouchera sur d’autres collaborations avec les collectivités territoriales du Pôle sud en général et de Bignona en particulier ». Lamine Niang est revenu sur le magazine « Soleil du Sud ». À son avis, ce projet a pour but de mettre en lumière les spécificités de la zone dans les domaines de l’économie, de la culture, du tourisme, etc. Également, il a mis en exergue le fait qu’à travers son réseau de correspondants dans cette zone, « Le Soleil » contribue pleinement au rayonnement de la Casamance. Développer les terroirs Dans le cadre de la mise en place des Pôles territoires, avec pour objectif de réussir à impulser un développement local, M. Niang pense que le « Soleil du Sud » peut servir de pont pour la vulgarisation des richesses économiques et culturelles de la Casamance et, par ricochet, attirer davantage d’investisseurs ». « Dans notre politique, la partie sud du pays occupe une place importante et avec la publication « Soleil du Sud », nous évoquons les atouts des terroirs, mais également les écueils qui plombent son essor », a dit le Dg de la Sspp « Le Soleil ». Ce dernier a aussi évoqué les efforts des autorités à travers le « Plan Diomaye pour la Casamance », qui aide à la réinstallation des personnes déplacées par le conflit, mais travaille également au développement des régions de Ziguinchor, Sédhiou et Kolda. Pour Alphousseny Diémé, maire de la commune de Djinaky, ce partenariat permettra de développer une communication pour renforcer l’efficacité de leurs actions. D’après lui, le choix du quotidien national « Le Soleil » comme support de communication n’est pas anodin. Il émane, selon lui, « de la grandeur de l’institution, de son poids historique et de son héritage dans le paysage médiatique sénégalais ». De plus, a-t-il fait savoir, le choix s’est basé sur l’offre de service du journal « Le Soleil » avec une large gamme de productions qui touche aux questions liées à l’essor des territoires. M. Diémé estime, en effet, que ce partenariat va jeter les bases d’un développement durable dans leur localité à travers la promotion de leurs richesses tout en contribuant à mettre en lumière leurs problèmes. « La commune de Djinaky est confrontée à un retard infrastructurel, avec un manque criant de routes. L’accès est difficile et beaucoup de nos localités restent isolées. C’est tout le sens de ce partenariat qui va nous aider à mettre en lumière ces questions, afin que l’on puisse trouver des solutions », a souligné le maire. Bada MBATHIE

items.title: From Jewellery Box to Cash: What Makes Gold Earrings Valuable?
items.description: A pair of gold earrings may be worth more than they look. Value depends on purity, weight, hallmark and condition; gemstones, a designer name or antique features can add to it beyond the metal itself. How a buyer tests and prices the pair matters too, particularly if you are deciding whether to sell gold for cash or keep an unused pair in the drawer. This guide explains what affects the value of earrings, how UK hallmarking works and what to check before accepting an offer. It also looks at why one buyer’s quote can differ from another’s. What Gives Gold Earrings Their Value? The first thing a buyer looks at is the amount and purity of gold in the earrings. Gold jewellery is made by combining gold with other metals, so two pairs that look almost identical can contain very different amounts of precious metal. The hallmark can help establish the purity of the gold. Weight is also important, although the full weight of an earring may include stones, posts, backs and other materials that are not gold. A buyer may therefore calculate the offer using the actual gold content rather than the total weight of the pair. This is where an old pair of earrings can become interesting. What may appear to be an ordinary item at the back of a jewellery box could contain a meaningful amount of gold, particularly if the earrings are heavier or made from higher-purity metal. Their value can also be higher if they have qualities that make them desirable as finished jewellery. Why Does Weight Matter? Purity tells you the proportion of gold. Weight tells you how much material is being assessed. Both are needed to understand the metal value. The total weight can be misleading because earrings may include gemstone settings, posts, backs or springs made from different materials. A buyer assessing the metal may therefore use the gold-bearing weight rather than the full weight. Ask how an offer has been calculated. A valuation based on gross weight is not necessarily comparable with one based on recoverable gold content. What Does a UK Hallmark Tell You? A hallmark is one of the clearest indicators of precious-metal purity in Britain. A full UK hallmark contains a sponsor’s or maker’s mark, a fineness mark and an Assay Office mark. A date letter can also appear, although it is optional. The four UK Assay Offices are Birmingham, Edinburgh, London and Sheffield. They test precious-metal articles and apply recognised hallmarks when the required standard is met. A 2026 YouGov survey commissioned by the four UK Assay Offices found that only 52% of more than 2,000 adults were confident they understood what a hallmark meant. Once its purpose was explained, 92% said hallmarking was important when buying precious-metal jewellery. For someone assessing old earrings, the hallmark can help establish the metal standard. It does not, however, determine the resale price. Are Gold-Plated Earrings Worth the Same? No. Gold-plated jewellery has a layer of gold over another material, so it should not be valued in the same way as solid gold. UK hallmarking guidance contains specific rules for describing precious-metal articles and gold-plated silver. A gold-coloured surface does not establish that an item is solid gold. Small earrings also need extra attention. Gold articles weighing less than 1 gram are exempt from compulsory hallmarking in the UK. Therefore, an unhallmarked lightweight earring is not automatically imitation jewellery. What Should You Check Before Selling Gold Earrings? Before accepting an offer to sell gold for cash, find out exactly what the buyer is paying for. The following checks can make different quotations easier to compare: Check the hallmark and fineness. Weigh the earrings, allowing for non-gold components. Ask whether gemstones are assessed separately. Find out which gold rate is used. Check whether testing, refining, postage or other costs are deducted. Understand whether an estimate can change after inspection. Read the payment and delivery terms before sending jewellery. The advertised rate per gram is only one part of the calculation. Purity, payable weight and the buyer’s valuation method will influence the final amount. How Are Gold Earrings Tested Before Valuation? A buyer needs to know how much gold is actually in a pair of earrings before deciding what they are worth. A clear hallmark can provide useful information. But testing may be needed when the markings are worn, difficult to read or missing. The common methods for valuation are as follows: X-ray fluorescence (XRF): This is a non-destructive test that checks the metal composition without damaging the earrings. It can identify the gold content and fineness, and the Goldsmiths’ Company Assay Office says the process can take less than 30 seconds in many cases. Assay testing: Professional assay offices can test precious-metal articles to establish whether they meet the required fineness standard. This forms part of the hallmarking process used in the UK. Visual inspection: A buyer may examine hallmarks, maker’s marks, clasps, posts and other features alongside testing. This can help identify whether an item may have additional value as a finished piece. For anyone planning to sell gold for cash , testing matters because the final offer may be based on confirmed gold content rather than appearance or the stated description of the earrings. This is also why an initial estimate can change after the jewellery has been received and assessed. Which Buyer Is Right for Your Earrings? The route depends on what gives the earrings value. Damaged or incomplete earrings may mainly be worth their gold content. A complete pair with diamonds, an established maker or antique appeal may be better suited to a jewellery-focused valuation. Before deciding to sell gold for cash , identify the features that could influence the price. This can explain why two buyers may offer different amounts for the same earrings. A clear valuation should show how the figure was decided. Conclusion The value of gold earrings depends on more than their looks. The purity and weight of the gold matter most, but the brand, gemstones, design and condition can also affect the price. A hallmark can help you check the gold content. Before you decide to sell gold for cash , check your earrings properly and understand how the buyer has worked out the offer. This will help you know whether the price you are being offered is fair for the jewellery you have. The post From Jewellery Box to Cash: What Makes Gold Earrings Valuable? appeared first on Vanguard News .

Carrick stays but senior Man Utd figures concerned by performances — Report
items.description: By Adegboyega Adeleye Manchester United head coach Michael Carrick is set to remain in charge for Sunday’s Premier League clash against Bournemouth despite growing concern among senior club figures over the team’s performances and results. According to the BBC, Carrick is continuing as normal and has not been informed of any imminent change following United’s humiliating 4-1 defeat by Como in the Champions League on Wednesday. However, the club has begun identifying potential replacements. One source told BBC Sport: “We need to work hard to get through it.” Another acknowledged that the team’s injury problems had affected performances but insisted they were “no excuse”, describing the players’ effort levels as “concerning”. “We have a Champions League squad and need to be playing at that level,” the source added. Despite the concerns, some figures within United believe the club’s repeated changes of manager in recent years have failed to reverse its decline. They also believe Carrick has been let down by players who have failed to perform to expectations. Fernandes questions Carrick’s tactics United captain Bruno Fernandes questioned Carrick’s tactics following Wednesday’s defeat, adding to the scrutiny surrounding the head coach. The loss to Como extended United’s winless run to seven matches in all competitions, with the club having recorded just two victories in their last 11 games. Defender Lisandro Martinez has also recently criticised aspects of the club’s recruitment, while former manager Erik ten Hag spoke of “broken promises” and a “toxic culture” in an interview with The Athletic. United have struggled at both ends of the pitch this season, scoring inconsistently and keeping just one clean sheet, while injuries and declining confidence have compounded their problems. The club’s current run is its worst since the 2015-16 season, when an eight-match winless streak put former manager Louis van Gaal under intense pressure. Man Utd consider potential replacements Although Carrick is expected to lead United against Bournemouth, the club has started identifying possible successors as uncertainty over his longer-term future continues. Former Newcastle United manager Eddie Howe, former Chelsea boss Antonio Conte and ex-Germany coach Julian Nagelsmann are understood to be among those being considered. Aston Villa manager Unai Emery and Brighton head coach Fabian Hurzeler are also admired by influential figures at Old Trafford, although securing their departures from their respective clubs could prove difficult. Carrick was appointed permanently in May after winning 12 of his 17 matches as interim manager and helping United return to the Champions League following a two-year absence. However, the club’s hierarchy remains concerned about the team’s current performances, with some believing Carrick deserves more time while others are dissatisfied with the results. United’s players were given Thursday off and are expected to return to training on Friday, when Carrick will address the media ahead of Sunday’s Premier League match against Bournemouth. Bournemouth won their first Premier League match under manager Marco Rose last week. They drew 4-4 at Old Trafford last season and won their previous two visits to the ground 3-0.
