items.title: Sex therapist calls for national sexuality education policy in Ghana
items.description: A US-trained sex therapist, Joshua Kwame Yeboah, has called on the government and stakeholders to develop a national sexuality education policy to address gaps in public understanding and strengthen professional practice in Ghana. Mr Yeboah, Founder and Chief Executive Officer of the Institute of Sexuality, Marriage and Family Life Research and Training (iSMART), said sexuality remained difficult to discuss constructively in many homes, schools, churches and communities. “In some homes, schools, churches and communities, sexuality remains too uncomfortable to discuss constructively. Young people may be warned against sexual activity without being adequately equipped to understand puberty, personal boundaries, consent, abuse prevention and responsible decision-making,” he said. “The challenge is not simply whether we discuss sexuality. It is whether we discuss it accurately, responsibly and constructively.” He was speaking at a graduation ceremony in Accra on October 17, 2026, for the first cohort of students to complete iSMART’s International Professional Certificate in Sex Therapy programme. The ceremony was held under the theme, “The New Sexual Revolution: Professionalising Sex Therapy Practice in Africa.” It also sought to promote professional competence, responsible communication and institutional accountability in sexuality education and sex therapy. Calls for renewed debate on sexuality education Mr Yeboah urged Ghana to revisit the Comprehensive Sexuality Education (CSE) proposal introduced in 2019, which was halted following concerns from parents, stakeholders and sections of the public. He argued that scientific knowledge could be integrated with Ghanaian cultural and religious values to support a more comprehensive approach to sexuality education. “I therefore advocate for a Ghanaian, culturally sensitive, faith-informed and scientifically grounded framework for holistic sexuality education,” he said. He proposed that the framework should provide age-appropriate education on bodily development, personal safety, consent, abuse prevention, healthy relationships, reproductive health and responsible decision-making. Mr Yeboah also urged sexuality professionals to use social media to share credible information and counter misinformation, saying this would help break the silence surrounding sexuality. Proposal for African Academy of Sex Therapy Board Chairman of iSMART and former UNESCO director, Reverend Dr Emmanuel Apea, proposed the establishment of an African Academy of Sex Therapy and Sexual Health to support the development of the profession across the continent. He said the proposed academy could bring together qualified professionals, researchers, educators and trainers to establish common professional standards, ethical guidelines, supervised practice and continuing professional development programmes. The initiative, he said, would also encourage research and collaboration among African countries. “This is indeed possible, because I recall that years ago during my presidency at the Ghana Association of Science Teachers, we were able to form both the West African Association of Science Teachers and the Forum of African Science Educators,” Rev. Dr Apea said. He urged universities, healthcare organisations, training institutions and professional associations to support the initiative by working out its structure, membership requirements and quality assurance processes. Calls for professional training in sex therapy A lecturer at the University of Cape Coast and iSMART board member, Professor Stephen Doh Fia, also called for misconceptions about sexuality education and sex therapy to be addressed. He challenged the claim that Ghanaian culture did not traditionally teach sex and therefore sexuality education should not be introduced. “Culture did talk about sex through Dipo, Brago and puberty rites,” he said, referring to traditional rites associated with puberty and social development. Prof. Fia further advocated the introduction of postgraduate certificate programmes or specialised courses in psychosexual therapy within university Clinical Psychology and Counselling Psychology programmes. The proposals come amid calls from sexuality professionals for more structured education, training and ethical standards to improve public understanding of sexuality and strengthen professional practice in Ghana.

items.title: Protect vulnerable girls, not GES reputation – Dr Kwabena Tandoh
items.description: Former Deputy Director-General of the Ghana Education Service (GES), Dr Kwabena B. Tandoh, has urged educational leaders to prioritise protecting vulnerable girls in schools rather than focus on safeguarding the reputation of the service and other educational institutions. Speaking on The Pulse with Fostina Sarfo, he said allegations of abuse exposed through documentaries should prompt a broader examination of the systems responsible for protecting children in schools. “I think I first need to state clearly that our responsibility as educational leaders is not to protect the GES or educational institutions, but to protect the vulnerable girls who sit in our classrooms,” he said. Dr Tandoh stressed that revelations of abuse should not automatically be treated as the final account of events but should trigger further scrutiny of the institutions responsible for safeguarding students. “If a documentary uncovers such abuse, it does not mean that the initial report should be taken as the final truth. Rather, it should be seen as a glaring symptom of an ill-equipped system,” he said. He argued that the focus should be on whether the education system has the capacity to protect children and respond appropriately to allegations of misconduct. “It is a symptom of an ill-equipped system to really protect children and to really take care of what needs to be done in the schools,” he added. Dr Tandoh also questioned the scope of the committee established by the GES following the violent demonstrations on August 4 and 5. While describing the committee as a positive administrative step, he said its mandate must be understood within the circumstances that led to its formation. “One other thing we need to quickly be thinking about is the committee that was put together by the GES. It’s a very good committee, but we need to understand that it is an administrative committee,” he said. According to him, the committee was established specifically in response to the demonstrations and tasked with investigating the circumstances that led to the unrest. “It was put together specifically as a reaction to a violent demonstration that happened on August 4 and 5. And so that committee’s mandate was to look into what caused the demonstrations,” he said. He noted that the committee’s work was therefore limited by its terms of reference. “The committee had a limited scope, and the committee itself stated that its scope and its mandate were limited,” he added. Dr Tandoh’s comments underscore the distinction between an administrative inquiry into student demonstrations and the broader responsibility of education authorities to ensure schools are safe environments for children. He said the priority should be to examine weaknesses in child-protection systems and ensure that allegations of abuse receive appropriate attention, rather than allowing concerns about institutional reputation to overshadow student welfare.

Des pourparlers seraient en cours pour obtenir la liberation des deux derniers enleves. Le premier enlevement a eu lieu le mardi 20 octobre, vers 15 heures. Il concerne le directeur du premier cycle de Fani, dans le cercle de Yangasso selon le responsable syndical. Deux autres enseignants ont ensuite ete enleves le mercredi 21 octobre, a environ 30 a 40 kilometres de la ville de San, Poursuit-t-il. « Le directeur et un enseignant, il y a trois enlevements en 48 heures », a declare Tiekoura Coulibaly, qui exprime son inquietude face a cette situation. Des menaces contre le fonctionnement des ecoles D'apres le porte-parole regional de la Synergie, ces enlevements seraient lies a des menaces visant le fonctionnement des etablissements scolaires. Il affirme que les informations recueillies par les syndicats font etat d'exigences concernant l'enseignement de l'arabe ou la fermeture des ecoles. « La cause que nous connaissons, c'est que soit vous enseignez l'arabe, soit l'ecole est fermee », a-t-il explique. Concernant les deux enseignants enleves le mercredi 21 octobre, des pourparlers seraient en cours en vue de leur liberation. La Synergie des syndicats de l'education souhaite que les trois collegues retrouvent rapidement leurs familles. « Securisation des ecoles » « Nous voulons que vraiment nos trois collegues reviennent sains et saufs », a insiste Tiekoura Coulibaly. Face a ces enlevements, la Synergie appelle les autorites a renforcer la securite dans les etablissements scolaires et a prendre des mesures pour proteger les enseignants. items.title: Nile University of Nigeria Inducts 75 New Medical Doctors at 5th MBBS Attestation Ceremony
items.description: Nile University of Nigeria has inducted 75 new medical doctors into the medical profession at its 5th MBBS Attestation Ceremony in Abuja, bringing the total number of doctors produced by the University since the inception of its MBBS programme to 257. The graduates, members of the University’s Class of 2025/2026, took the Physician’s Oath on Wednesday, 21 October 2026, following years of academic study and clinical training at the University’s College of Health Sciences. The ceremony marked a significant milestone for the graduates as they prepare to apply their training in professional practice. Four graduates stood out for their academic performance, recording multiple Pass with Distinction results across key medical disciplines. Abubakar Dahiru Bobo achieved seven distinctions, Shuaib Sanni Farida recorded five, while Sadi Abdu Fatima and Hafsa Awwal Abubakar each earned four. Delivering the attestation lecture, the Medical Elder, Professor Ahmed Ahidjo, former Chief Medical Director of the University of Maiduguri Teaching Hospital, drew on his professional experience to emphasise the importance of discipline, mentorship and continuous learning in medicine. He also discussed advances in interventional radiology and the role of innovation in medical practice, highlighting the need for doctors to keep abreast of developments in their field. The Registrar of the Medical and Dental Council of Nigeria (MDCN), Professor Fatima Kyari, administered the Physician’s Oath and commended the University’s contribution to medical education. She urged the graduates to look beyond individual achievement and consider how they could mentor others and contribute to national development through their profession. “Start to think about today. How you will make others grow, in this profession and in the country at large,” she said. The Vice-Chancellor of Nile University of Nigeria, Prof. Dilli Dogo, FNAMed, DFMC, reminded the graduates that completing their training was the beginning of a career that would demand dedication, accountability and service. “The journey starts now. It’s a journey of service, dedication, commitment and delivery,” he said. He urged them to honour the commitments they had made in taking the Physician’s Oath, stressing the responsibility that comes with the trust placed in medical professionals. “You are called to a profession that does not tolerate excuses. I urge you to stand by the oath you’ve taken,” he added. The Vice-Chancellor also highlighted the University’s international academic links, noting that it has partnerships with 126 universities worldwide. As the graduates prepare to begin the next stage of their careers, they also received medical starter tools to support their transition into professional practice. The induction of this fifth cohort reflects Nile University of Nigeria’s continuing contribution to medical education and the development of healthcare professionals in Nigeria. items.title: Ebola: Idris directs agencies to intensify public enlightenment
items.description: — Minister urges accurate information, warns against spreading unverified reports By Chidinma Chukwu ABUJA — The Minister of Information and National Orientation, Mohammed Idris, has directed agencies under his ministry to intensify public enlightenment on Ebola Virus Disease (EVD) following reports of a confirmed case in the Federal Capital Territory (FCT). The directive was issued to the National Orientation Agency (NOA), Nigerian Television Authority (NTA), Federal Radio Corporation of Nigeria (FRCN), Voice of Nigeria (VON) and News Agency of Nigeria (NAN). The minister’s Special Assistant on Media, Rabiu Ibrahim, disclosed this in a statement issued in Abuja on Thursday. According to the statement, Idris directed the agencies to work with relevant health authorities to ensure that Nigerians receive accurate, timely and evidence-based information about the disease. The Nigeria Centre for Disease Control and Prevention (NCDC) reportedly confirmed the case earlier this week in a woman who recently travelled to Abuja from Uganda. The woman is said to be in isolation and receiving treatment, while health authorities have identified her contacts and commenced follow-up measures. Reacting to the development, Idris said the Federal Government was taking necessary steps to contain the case and protect public health. “The Federal Government is taking every necessary step to contain this case and protect Nigerians. Accurate and timely information is one of our strongest defences. “Our agencies must reach every community, in every language, with clear facts on how Ebola spreads, how to protect ourselves and where to report suspected cases,” he said. The minister directed the agencies to collaborate with the Federal Ministry of Health and Social Welfare and the NCDC to ensure that public enlightenment campaigns are guided by verified information and established health advice. He specifically tasked the NOA with deploying its nationwide network of offices for grassroots sensitisation. The agency is expected to work with traditional and religious leaders, community groups and the media to ensure that accurate information reaches people at the community level. Idris also urged Nigerians to remain calm, rely on official sources and refrain from circulating unverified reports and claims on social media. Members of the public were advised to report suspected cases through the NCDC’s toll-free, 24-hour emergency line on 6232. items.title: Désenclavement des zones rurales : Les pistes réhabilitées dans le cadre du PAPR 1 ouvertes aux usagers
items.description: Blitta, 22 oct. (ATOP) – Les pistes réhabilitées dans le pays, dans le cadre de la phase 1 du Programme d’appui aux pistes rurales (PAPR1), ont été officiellement, ouvertes aux usagers le mercredi 21 octobre dans la commune Blitta 2. L’ouverture de ces voies aux populations a été symbolisée par l’inauguration du tronçon Atikpai-Foudjayé-Niamtougou Copé-Tcharébaou-Aféma-Sala Kopé. La cérémonie inaugurale a été co-présidée par le ministre des Transports, du désenclavement et des pistes rurales, Komlan Loukou-Kadjè, le ministre conseiller du Président du Conseil, Etsri Homevor et la chargée de Coopération avec le Togo auprès de la BMZ en Allemagne, Mme Anne Rehner. La réhabilitation de ces pistes permettra de renforcer l’accès aux zones rurales, d’améliorer les mobilités des populations et de stimuler le développement économique et social local. Vue partielle de la piste inaugurale Initié en 2017, le PAPR s’inscrit dans le cadre d’un grand projet de désenclavement des zones rurales, en soutien à la politique de développement du secteur agricole au Togo. Il est conjointement financé par l’Etat togolais, l’Allemagne, à travers sa Banque de développement (KfW) et la France, via son Agence de développement (AFD). D’un coût de 23,21 milliards de FCFA, le PAPR 1 couvre les zones à fort potentiel de production de coton et de café-cacao. Il vise la réhabilitation de 935 km de pistes rurales dont le tronçon inaugural distant de 32 km. D’un coût de 980 millions de FCFA, cette voie va désenclaver les six villages desservis. Elle favorisera, entre autres, l’écoulement rapide des produits agricoles vers les marchés et l’accès facile aux services de santé et à l’éducation. Evalué à 35, 54 milliards de FCFA, le PAPR 2, en phase de démarrage, porte sur l’aménagement de 846 km de pistes rurales réparti dans toutes les régions du pays. L’évènement a permis aux officiels de visiter le tronçon inaugural, de recevoir les explications sur les travaux réalisés et de suivre un film documentaire révélant les avantages des pistes rurales pour les populations. Le ministre Loukou-Kadjè a fait savoir que la réhabilitation de ces pistes constitue un enjeu crucial pour le pays. Il a souligné que « dans le contexte mondial actuel, marqué par les exigences de souveraineté, de résilience et de progrès social, le Président du Conseil, appelle à une mobilisation collective, pour bâtir un Togo plus uni et tourné, résolument, vers l’avenir ». Le ministre a rassuré les partenaires de l’entretien des ouvrages pour leur pérennité. Mme Anne Rehner a, au nom des partenaires, exprimé, sa satisfaction pour la qualité des travaux exécutés. Elle a souhaité que ces pistes contribuent au renforcement de l’activité économique et à l’amélioration des conditions de vie des populations. Le préfet de Blitta, Anakpa Mani et le maire de Blitta 2, Malou Kodjo ont affirmé que la réhabilitation du tronçon susmentionné figure parmi les besoins prioritaires des populations, ce qui vient combler l’une de leurs attentes. Mme Anne Rehner était accompagnée d’une délégation composée de ses collègues de l’ambassade d’Allemagne au Togo avec en tête l’ambassadeur, Stefan Messerer ainsi que des directeurs résidents de la KFW, de la GIZ et de l’AFD au Togo. La cérémonie a pris fin par la coupure du ruban symbolique par M. Etri Homevor et les autres officiels. ATOP/MEK/BA

items.title: ‘We were lucky to win everything’ – Messi reflects on his years at Barcelona
items.description: Barcelona legend Lionel Messi has reflected on his remarkable spell at the Spanish club, describing his time at Camp Nou as difficult to put into words. Messi returned to Spain to collect the 2026 Princess of Asturias Award for Sports at a ceremony in Oviedo, where he spoke about his memories of playing alongside some of Barcelona’s greatest stars. The Argentine, widely regarded as one of football’s greatest players, recalled sharing a dressing room with Xavi Hernandez, Andres Iniesta and Carles Puyol, highlighting the trophies they won and the enjoyment they experienced both on and off the pitch. “It was a privilege to share a dressing room with Xavi, Iniesta, Puyol and so many others. We were fortunate enough to win everything, and to do it the way we did: how much we enjoyed playing, winning and achieving great things. But above all, we enjoyed our day-to-day life, the training sessions; we had a wonderful time,” he told EFE. Reflecting further on his time at the club, Messi said his experiences in Barcelona left him with lasting memories and a special emotional connection to both the city and the team. “It is difficult to sum up in a few words. I experienced so many incredible moments and obviously hold a very, very special affection for both the city and the club.” Messi was announced as the recipient of the award earlier this year, becoming the first individual footballer to receive the honour from the Princess of Asturias Awards committee. The committee recognised not only his achievements on the pitch but also his sustained charitable efforts to improve access to education and healthcare for disadvantaged children. “In addition to his dazzling talent, his exceptional sporting career and his remarkable and sustained charitable work to promote access to education and healthcare for the most disadvantaged children,” a statement read. The award committee also praised Messi’s conduct, humility and commitment to teamwork throughout his illustrious career. “Leo Messi, the player who has won the most titles in the history of football, has also earned the respect and admiration of everyone for his exemplary behaviour on the field and for his consistency, humility and commitment to the team game.” Vanguard News The post ‘We were lucky to win everything’ – Messi reflects on his years at Barcelona appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: Bourse de Casablanca : clôture sur une note positive
items.description: La Bourse de Casablanca a terminé sur une note positive jeudi, son indice principal, le MASI, gagnant 0,74% à 17.134,15 points (pts). Le MASI 20, qui regroupe les 20 valeurs les plus liquides, a pris 0,9% à 1.244,21 pts et le MASI ESG, indice des entreprises ayant la meilleure notation ESG selon Moody’s ESG Solutions, a avancé de 0,6% à 1.263,06 pts. Le MASI Mid and Small Cap, reflétant la performance des petites et moyennes entreprises cotées, a, quant à lui, progressé de 1,12% à 1.629,3 pts. Sur le plan sectoriel, les indices « Assurances » (+3,1%), « Pétrole et gaz » (+2,4%) et « Ingénieries et biens d’équipement industriels » (+2,1%) ont signé les meilleures performances. À l’inverse, les secteurs « Sylviculture et papier » (-2,71%), « Mines » (-0,85%) et « Distributeurs » (-0,35%) ont enregistré les plus fortes baisses. Le volume global des échanges s’est établi à plus de 196,87 millions de dirhams (MDH). Les transactions les plus importantes ont porté sur Attijariwafa Bank, avec un volume de 31,68 MDH, Bank of Africa (30,58 MDH) et Managem (18,77 MDH). La capitalisation boursière a, quant à elle, dépassé 1.006,73 milliards de dirhams. Aux valeurs individuelles, les plus fortes progressions ont été enregistrées par Maghreb Oxygène (+9,77% à 382 DH), Sanlam Maroc (+7,42% à 3.099 DH), Lesieur Cristal (+5,45% à 290 DH), Bank of Africa (+5,06% à 184,8 DH) et Jet Contractors (+4,76% à 1.498 DH). À l’opposé, Colorado (-4,49% à 73,55 DH), Med Paper (-2,71% à 21,5 DH), M2M Group (-2,5% à 390 DH), Mutandis (-2,18% à 215,2 DH) et la Compagnie Minière de Touissit (-1,95% à 4.020 DH) ont accusé les plus fortes baisses. items.title: CROUS Sine Saloum: Les syndicalistes dénoncent le recours à la réquisition !
items.description: Les partenaires sociaux déplorent le recours à la réquisition et réclament des explications à la direction sur cette mesure prise en pleine crise sociale. Le climat social reste tendu au Centre régional des œuvres universitaires sociales du Sine Saloum (CROUS-SS). Dans une déclaration, les partenaires sociaux dénoncent le recours à la réquisition des travailleurs, qu’ils considèrent comme une entrave au dialogue social. Ils estiment que la direction privilégie la contrainte au détriment de la concertation. Au cœur de la polémique, l’arrêté n° 0154/GR.KAF/BC du gouverneur de Kaffrine, daté du 21 octobre 2026. Selon les syndicats, ce texte fait suite à une lettre adressée la veille par le directeur du CROUS Sine Saloum, sollicitant la réquisition d’agents pour la période du 21 au 23 octobre. Une démarche que les représentants des travailleurs regrettent, estimant qu’une concertation aurait dû être privilégiée face aux revendications soulevées. Autre point de contestation, les lettres de notification n’auraient été reçues que le mercredi 21 octobre à 18 h 30, alors que l’arrêté fixait les horaires de réquisition de 8 h à 18 h pour cette même journée. Les syndicats demandent ainsi à la direction de préciser les modalités de comptabilisation de cette journée. Ils exigent également la communication de la lettre ayant motivé la mesure ainsi que la justification de chaque poste réquisitionné au regard du décret n° 72-017 du 11 janvier 1972. Tout en appelant les agents concernés à se conformer à la réquisition pendant la période indiquée, les partenaires sociaux se réservent le droit d’engager des recours pour défendre le droit de grève. Les syndicats réitèrent, par ailleurs, leurs principales doléances, notamment les rétrogradations qu’ils jugent arbitraires, le paiement sélectif de certaines primes et les affectations contestées. « Le directeur peut faire réquisitionner des agents, mais il ne peut réquisitionner ni le cœur ni la voix des travailleurs », préviennent-ils, réaffirmant leur détermination à défendre les droits syndicaux et à obtenir des réponses à leurs revendications. Mamadou THIAM ( Correspondant)

items.title: Many Nigerians can afford houses with right priorities — Ojiribe
items.description: — Raphmaths Estates boss says some prioritise luxury cars over land By Chimaobi Nwaiwu NNEWI — The Chairman and Chief Executive Officer of Raphmaths Estates, Chief Raphael Ojiribe, has said that some Nigerians who consider themselves low-income earners and unable to afford homes could improve their chances of property ownership by prioritising their spending. Ojiribe said many people, particularly young Nigerians, preferred spending money on luxury cars and other expensive personal items rather than investing in land, which he said could appreciate in value over time. He spoke with journalists in his office in Onitsha, Anambra State, on Wednesday while responding to questions about housing shortages in urban areas despite the growing presence of property developers, as well as concerns over the affordability of homeownership for low-income earners. According to him, some people classified as low-income earners could own property if they exercised greater financial discipline and took advantage of available payment plans. “Many people that are classified as low-income earners can actually afford to own houses of their own, but the problem with many is that they do not know how to set their priorities right,” he said. Ojiribe cited the example of people who spend about ₦15 million on cars instead of investing the money in land, arguing that such spending decisions could limit their ability to acquire property. “Many people, particularly young boys, prefer to use ₦15 million to buy a car instead of investing the money in land. Can you call such people low-income earners?” he asked. The estate developer said Raphmaths Estates had introduced payment plans intended to make land purchases more accessible to buyers with different financial capacities. He, however, urged prospective buyers to take advantage of such arrangements and begin investing when opportunities arose. Citing the company’s Sea View Estate in Awka, Anambra State, Ojiribe said the estate was launched for sales in February at ₦15 million per plot. He said the company had reduced its prices at the time to encourage low- and middle-income earners to acquire land, adding that the price of a plot had since risen to between ₦25 million and ₦30 million. According to him, buyers who invested at the initial price could have recorded substantial gains based on the current asking prices. Ojiribe said the price adjustment was intended to encourage early investment and that buyers across different income brackets had benefited from the promotional offer. He maintained that some people who complained about being unable to afford homes could reconsider their spending choices, noting that expensive vehicle purchases did not necessarily translate into long-term asset ownership. However, the affordability of housing also depends on income levels, land prices, access to mortgage financing and other living costs, factors that can limit the ability of low-income households to buy property even when they manage their spending carefully. The post Many Nigerians can afford houses with right priorities — Ojiribe appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: L’Ansts souligne l’importance de l’intégrité intellectuelle à l’ère de l’IA
items.description: L’Académie nationale des sciences et techniques du Sénégal (Ansts), en partenariat avec l’Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar (Ucad), a invité mercredi, les chercheurs à placer l’éthique et l’intégrité intellectuelle au cœur de leurs travaux à l’ère de l’intelligence artificielle générative. L’éthique au cœur de la recherche scientifique. C’est le message porté par l’Académie nationale des sciences et techniques du Sénégal (Ansts) lors de la célébration de la Journée mondiale de l’éthique, organisée, hier, en partenariat avec l’Université Cheikh Anta Diop de Dakar (Ucad), à travers l’École doctorale Études sur l’homme et la société (Ed-Ethos) et la direction de l’animation culturelle et scientifique. La rencontre a réuni des doctorants et de jeunes chercheurs autour des enjeux de l’intégrité scientifique dans un contexte marqué par le développement rapide de l’Intelligence artificielle (Ia). Pour le professeur Anta Tall Dia, membre de la commission éthique et déontologie de l’Ansts, le sujet répond à une préoccupation actuelle : l’usage de l’Ia générative dans les différentes étapes de la recherche, de la collecte et de l’analyse des données à la publication des résultats. « L’éthique sert à nous guider, c’est une boussole pour voir en matière de recherche, qu’est-ce qui est bien et qu’est-ce qui est mal », a-t-elle souligné. Selon elle, l’utilisation de cet outil doit s’accompagner d’une vigilance particulière pour prévenir le plagiat, la manipulation des données et la publication de résultats erronés, car, soulignant que les travaux scientifiques ne sont pas sans conséquences sur la société. «Si les résultats de la recherche sont manipulés ou falsifiés, cela peut mener à de mauvaises décisions de la part des pouvoirs publics », a-t-elle averti, évoquant les controverses scientifiques apparues pendant la pandémie de Covid-19. Elle a également insisté sur le rôle des comités d’éthique et des instances de révision scientifique dans le contrôle des publications et le retrait des articles jugés non fiables. Pour Mme Dia, l’intelligence artificielle demeure un outil utile, mais ne peut se substituer au jugement humain ni aux valeurs de responsabilité, de justice et d’honnêteté. Selon le Pr Ramatoulaye Diagne Mbengue, présidente de la commission Ethique de l’Ansts, l’objectif n’est pas d’interdire l’Ia mais d’apprendre aux étudiants et chercheurs de l’utiliser avec discernement. L’ancienne recteur de l’université de Thiès met en garde contre la tendance à présenter des contenus générés par l’intelligence artificielle comme des productions personnelles sans reconnaître leur origine. Une telle pratique risque, selon elle, d’affaiblir l’esprit critique et la capacité des chercheurs à développer leurs propres idées. Maguette Guèye DIÉDHIOU

items.title: Direct flights between Pakistan and Maldives on the horizon as PM stresses connectivity
items.description: Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday announced that he had issued instructions for direct flights between Pakistan and the Maldives. The premier was addressing the Pakistan-Maldives Business Forum, attended by visiting Maldivian President Dr Mohamed Muizzu, who arrived in Islamabad on Tuesday for a three-day trip at the invitation of PM Shehbaz. The visit marks the first by a Maldivian president to Pakistan in 11 years, and comes as the two countries celebrate the 60th anniversary of their diplomatic relations, established in 1966. PM Shehbaz said, “I want to say that connectivity is very important. We don’t have direct flights from Malé to Islamabad or Karachi, so this air link is very important. “I have already given instructions to our ministry of civil aviation to prepare a quick feasibility [study], be it Pakistan International Airlines, or any other airline in Pakistan, to find the ways and means to take the first flight comprising tourists [and the] business community to Malé,” he announced. The premier said he had been informed by President Muizzu that he gave instructions “to his airline to work out a quick plan to start flights from [the] Maldives to Pakistan”. “I have given instructions to our civil aviation department to immediately invite a delegation from [the] Maldives and work out a plan whereby we can start these air flights between the two countries as early as possible,” PM Shehbaz added. Moreover, the premier highlighted the importance of maritime connectivity, noting that unless there is a reliable direct shipping schedule from Karachi or Gwadar to Male, “we will not be able to meet our targets efficiently and effectively.” He added that once Muizzu returned to his country, a delegation of Pakistani government officials and businessmen would be sent to Malé. He said that the delegation would arrive within the next week or so. Calling Muizzu a “very sincere friend of Pakistan”, the premier hailed his visit as a “turning point in further strengthening our bilateral, brotherly relations” and a “game-changer in terms of promoting our bilateral trade and investment portfolios”. “I would like to convey this message to our great entrepreneurs, traders, investors and businessmen from both [the] Maldives and Pakistan,” he added. “Here is an opportunity we can really convert into … a concrete action plan.” Citing figures provided by Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan, PM Shehbaz said that the trade volume between Islamabad and Malé is approximately $13 million. “My brother, President Dr Muizzu, on my request, readily agreed to make a firm understanding to increase our bilateral trade from $13m to $200m in the next two years, and now it’s all up to us to make use of this opportunity, do our homework and make full preparation to achieve these targets through joint efforts and very close coordination,” the prime minister stated. Taking the podium, President Muizzu echoed PM Shehbaz and urged the establishment of an air corridor between Pakistan and the Maldives. “In this regard, I am pleased to announce that Maldivian, our national airline, aims to establish [a] direct air link between Male and Karachi soon,” he announced. “This service will make travel easier for the people of our two countries, creating new opportunities for trade and tourism.” He thanked PM Shehbaz for taking the time to attend the forum and said that his presence was “a testament to the close friendship and our shared commitment to strengthening economic cooperation”. “It is such a great pleasure for me to be with you today in Islamabad. And particularly to address a gathering of those who drive enterprise, investment, and economic opportunity in our two countries,” he added. “As we mark 60 years since the establishment of diplomatic relations, the relationship between the Maldives and Pakistan is rooted in deep fraternal affection, and above all, in the enduring bond of our Islamic faith.” Muizzu noted that while Islamabad and Male had strong political solidarity and diplomatic trust, their economic relationship had yet to reach its full potential. “We must now define the ambition of our future,” the Maldivian president said. “The time has come to transform the strength of our friendship into a new era of trade, investment, and shared prosperity, which is why yesterday Prime Minister Sharif and I agreed to enhance our bilateral trade to $200m over the next two years.” He added, “Beyond the numbers, this ambitious target is investing in our people. We are not only creating new opportunities for businesses on both sides, but also fostering greater regional prosperity and long-term stability.” Muizzu said Pakistan possessed tremendous potential and that the economies of both nations had “important complementarities”. “For the Maldives, food security is not merely a commercial consideration. As an island nation, resilient supply chains are a matter of national security, and the scale of our market should not be underestimated,” he explained. Noting that Pakistan’s agricultural sector already serves the island nation, Muizzu emphasised the need to move beyond a typical buyer and seller relationship into partnerships in cold chain logistics, temperature-controlled storage, modern food processing and climate-adaptive agricultural technology “But trade requires connectivity. For an island nation, maritime connectivity is an economic lifeline. We must create more efficient corridors through which that trade can move,” he highlighted. “Therefore, I encourage shipping, port and logistics companies from both countries to explore direct and commercially viable connections between Pakistan and the Maldives.” Stressing the importance of healthcare infrastructure, the Maldivian president highlighted that the country is making significant investments to move from regional tertiary hospitals to modern island-level facilities. “Our demand for reliable, high-quality and certified medical supplies will therefore continue to grow. We welcome Pakistani pharmaceutical manufacturers and healthcare providers,” Muizzu said. Furthermore, he invited Pakistan’s construction companies, developers, manufacturers and engineering firms to partner with the Maldives in housing, land reclamation and connectivity projects, as part of Male’s endeavours in infrastructure and urban development. “Renewable energy is another area of enormous potential. The Maldives spends hundreds of millions of dollars each year importing diesel. For us, therefore, the transition to clean energy is not only a climate imperative, it is an economic and fiscal necessity,” he added. “My administration has set a target of producing 33 per cent of our national electricity requirement from renewable sources by 2028. That means more than quadrupling more than the amount generated in a five-year period.” Additionally, the Maldivian president highlighted opportunities in both nations, unlocking the power of the global Islamic economy through Sharia-compliant finance, and halal tourism and products. “The Maldives is strengthening its financial landscape and institutional frameworks for Islamic finance,” he said. “Together, our financial institutions, regulators, and businesses can explore Sharia-compliant investment instruments, sukuk , Islamic financial services and halal value chains. And these areas are by no means exhaustive.” Muizzu also highlighted opportunities in tourism and hospitality, IT, education and other sectors and invited Pakistani businesses to “not look at the Maldives merely as a market to sell to, [but] look at the Maldives as a partner to build with”.

items.title: Tansian University crisis deepens as rival bodies claim ownership
items.description: — NUC recognises missionary group as proprietor, letter shows — Missionaries pledge to settle Ezeonwuka’s ₦10m annual honorarium arrears — Parents reportedly seek students’ safety as police barricade campuses By Nwabueze Okonkwo ONITSHA — The ownership crisis at Tansian University, Umunya, Anambra State, has deepened following competing claims over the institution’s control, with the National Universities Commission (NUC) recognising the Missionary Sons of the Blessed Tansi (MST) as its proprietor, according to a letter dated August 18, 2026. The dispute involves members of the missionary group, formerly known as the Missionary Servants of the Church (MSC), and Rev. Fr. Edwin Obiorah, a Senior Advocate of Nigeria (SAN), who currently occupies the position of Chancellor and Chairman of the university’s Board of Trustees. The latest development comes amid disagreements over the university’s registration, its leadership and an outstanding annual honorarium owed to Chief Rommy Ezeonwuka, who donated the institution’s take-off campus at Oba, in Idemili South Local Government Area of Anambra State. MST has reportedly terminated Obiorah’s legal representation and demanded that he hand over all files in his possession within seven days of the termination notice. In a letter jointly signed by the group’s coordinator, Rev. Dan Igwilo, and secretary, Bro. Paulde Silas Inuen, MST cited concerns over alleged conversion of institutional properties, allegedly misleading legal representations concerning the university, and what it described as the unauthorised assumption or exercise of authority in matters affecting the group. These remain allegations by the missionary group. The dispute has also extended to the appointment of the vice-chancellor. While MST reportedly wants Prof. Eugene Nwadialor retained in the position, Obiorah appointed Rev. Fr. Prof. Nnamdi Ambrose as his preferred candidate following the death of Prof. Cater Umeoduagu. Umeoduagu reportedly died about 24 hours after Obiorah appointed him acting vice-chancellor to take over from Nwadialor, who was abroad for a medical check-up. Tansian University was approved by the NUC in 2007. The ownership dispute reportedly intensified after the death of its founder, Monsignor John Bosco Akam, in 2021. Akam, a Catholic priest and founder of MSC, was said to have bequeathed the university to the missionary group in his will. NUC recognises MST In a statement dated August 18, 2026, and signed by its Director of Inspection and Monitoring, Mrs Justina Emerole, on behalf of the Executive Secretary, the NUC said it recognised MST as the proprietor of Tansian University, citing Sections 1(3) and 30 of the Tansian University Law, 2007. The commission also told the Commander of the Intelligence Response Team, Office of the Commissioner of Police, Force Intelligence Department, that it found no evidence that the names of Obiorah and members of his board had been forwarded for security clearance by the Department of State Services, as required under the relevant regulatory process. The letter, with reference number NUC/ES/15/Vol.2/449, was titled Re: Investigation Activities: Case of Criminal Conspiracy, Impersonation, Forgery, Attempted Murder and Fraud. The allegations listed in the title relate to an investigation and should not be taken as established findings against any individual. The commission said its efforts to restore peace at the university had yet to produce the desired results. “Our efforts at restoring peace in TANU over the years appears not yielding the desired fruits as evidenced by the recent crisis in the institution,” the letter stated. The NUC added that it had deployed an eight-member Forensic Audit Team to the university from June 21 to 28, 2026, to establish facts and recommend measures for resolving the dispute. It said the commission’s management was reviewing the team’s report before taking further action aimed at restoring stability and establishing a governance framework consistent with standards in Nigeria’s university system. Missionaries pledge to settle honorarium arrears Another longstanding dispute concerns the annual ₦10 million honorarium reportedly owed to Ezeonwuka for donating the property and structures used as the university’s take-off campus at Oba. According to the account provided by Ezeonwuka, an Anambra State High Court consent judgment directed the university’s management to pay him ₦10 million annually in recognition of the donation. The NUC reportedly approved the arrangement, stipulating that the payment should be described as an honorarium rather than rent for land, buildings or other property. The university paid the honorarium for some years but subsequently stopped, reportedly citing financial constraints. Ezeonwuka later obtained a judgment authorising the sale of movable and immovable university assets to recover the accumulated debt, according to the account provided. The university’s management under Obiorah challenged the judgment at the Court of Appeal. The appellate court reportedly upheld the lower court’s decision. The dispute is now before the Supreme Court, where Obiorah is challenging the decisions of the lower courts. Speaking by telephone, Ezeonwuka, who holds the title Ogilisi Igbo, said the unpaid honorarium had accumulated over more than 10 years. Rev. Val Onyelusi, a leader of MST, said the group was discussing with Ezeonwuka how to settle the outstanding amount once the missionary group regained control of the university. He said MST was prepared to honour the agreement on the annual honorarium. Onyelusi also alleged that Obiorah, who was engaged as the university’s lawyer by the late Akam, subsequently registered the institution as Tansian University Ltd/Gte and assumed the positions of chancellor and chairman of the Board of Trustees. The registration dispute remains central to the competing claims over the institution. Founder’s will cited MST also cited Akam’s will, dated October 5, 2014, which reportedly named the group as the owner of the university and the principal beneficiary of his estate. The will directed the university’s Governing Council, Board of Trustees, Pro-Chancellor and Vice-Chancellor to allocate 70 per cent of the institution’s profits to MST. The missionary group maintains that the document supports its claim to ownership and control of the university. Students caught in the dispute Meanwhile, students have reportedly been left stranded on campus amid heightened tensions, with parents seeking assurances about their children’s safety. The report said mobile policemen had barricaded the gates of both the Oba take-off campus and the main campus at Umunya. The situation has raised concerns about the disruption of academic activities and the welfare of students caught up in the ownership dispute. Efforts to obtain Obiorah’s response to MST’s termination of his legal representation and the NUC’s position on the university’s registration were unsuccessful before this report was filed. He could not be reached for comment. His response, as well as any further clarification from the university’s management, would be necessary to present the competing positions fully. The post Tansian University crisis deepens as rival bodies claim ownership appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: CSA and NITA order government institutions to fix critical PHP vulnerabilities within seven days
items.description: The Cyber Security Authority (CSA) and the National Information Technology Agency (NITA) have directed government institutions to address two critical vulnerabilities in PHP within seven days, warning that the flaws could allow attackers to take control of affected servers without a username or password. In a joint cybersecurity alert on Thursday, October 22, the agencies urged government institutions, businesses, website owners, hosting providers and operators of Critical Information Infrastructure to treat the threat as urgent and implement available security fixes. The vulnerabilities, identified as CVE-2026-109618 and CVE-2026-109619 and referred to as “PHP2Shell”, affect PHP, a programming language widely used to run websites and online services. Successful exploitation could expose sensitive information, disrupt digital services and allow attackers to launch further attacks against an organisation’s network. Security fixes available The agencies said the PHP Project had released fixes in versions 8.2.35, 8.3.36, 8.4.27 and 8.5.12. Affected organisations have been advised to install the appropriate patched release, upgrade to a later supported version or apply a vendor package confirmed to contain the fixes. They cautioned that updating website themes or plugins alone would not resolve vulnerabilities in the underlying PHP software. Seven-day deadline for government institutions Under the directive, all government institutions are required to take action within seven days and report the remedial measures taken to the CSA and NITA. Heads of institutions have been instructed to ensure that their information and communications technology (ICT) teams and service providers act urgently to identify and secure affected systems. NITA will coordinate technical support for government digital assets and services, while the CSA will oversee cybersecurity incident reporting and response. Institutions are also expected to maintain an up-to-date inventory of their digital assets and nominate responsible officers to support remediation and coordination under NITA’s Government Digital Assurance Programme (GovDAP). Five steps to protect digital systems The agencies have outlined five key measures for affected organisations. First, they should identify all websites, web applications and servers running PHP, including those managed by external service providers, prioritising internet-facing systems and essential public services. Second, they must apply the relevant security updates, follow vendor instructions, restart affected services where necessary and verify that the patches are working. Third, systems that cannot be updated immediately should be temporarily taken offline until they can be secured. Temporary protective measures should not replace permanent patching. Fourth, organisations should investigate possible compromises by reviewing system logs, unusual processes, unexpected administrator accounts and unauthorised changes to website files. Suspected compromised systems should be isolated and evidence preserved. Finally, website owners should obtain written confirmation from hosting providers, developers and system administrators that affected systems have been identified and patched. Public warned against fraudulent security updates The CSA and NITA have also cautioned the public against suspicious messages requesting downloads of purported “PHP security updates”, passwords or payment details. Website owners have been advised to obtain security updates only through official software sources or verified service providers. Where to report incidents Organisations and individuals who suspect a cybersecurity incident or system compromise can contact the CSA through the following channels: Call or SMS: 292 Email: report@csa.gov.gh For government digital services coordination and GovDAP enquiries, NITA can be contacted on: Email: govdap@nita.gov.gh Telephone: 055 249 9661 The agencies have urged all affected organisations to act immediately to protect sensitive information, maintain the availability of essential digital services and prevent further compromise of their systems.

items.title: À Paris, une manifestation interdite puis autorisée… mais condamnée à rester sur place
items.description: Le cortege devait rejoindre la Bastille depuis la Pitie-Salpetriere. La prefecture avait interdit son parcours, mais le tribunal administratif a leve cette interdiction le 22 octobre, apres un recours du collectif Interfac Île-de-France. Plusieurs milliers de manifestants se sont rassembles dans le sud-est de Paris, sous une forte presence policiere. La decision n'a pourtant pas rendu son parcours au cortege. D'apres l'Associated Press, les organisateurs ont signe un document de la police prevoyant que le rassemblement resterait statique, en raison des risques de violences. Une manifestation autorisee, donc, a condition de ne pas marcher. La justice dit oui, les restrictions restent La prefecture avait invoque les incidents survenus lors des mobilisations des 13 et 17 octobre. Un autre arrete continuait d'interdire le 22 octobre, de 8 heures a 20 heures, les rassemblements non declares dans plusieurs secteurs de Paris, notamment autour des institutions et des grandes gares. La decision du tribunal ne supprimait pas ces restrictions. Au meme moment, les regards se tournent deja vers le 24 octobre. Emmanuel Macron a annonce un durcissement des conditions de manifestation apres une reunion de securite a l'elysee. a Lyon, les rassemblements prevus ont ete interdits. Vitrines protegees, armureries debordees Dans le centre de Paris, des commercants font poser des panneaux de bois devant leurs vitrines. Le groupe Hermes a renforce la securite de ses boutiques francaises, rapporte Reuters. Cette fois, les magasins anticipent les risques avant la mobilisation, apres les pillages du 17 octobre . La mairie se prepare egalement. Depuis le 22 octobre, ses agents retirent les barrieres mobiles, les conteneurs et les objets pouvant servir a dresser des barricades. Les commercants sont invites a rentrer leur mobilier exterieur le 24 octobre a midi. Plus de 1 000 agents de la proprete seront mobilises pendant le week-end. Certains ne s'en remettent plus aux seules vitrines renforcees. Dans les armureries, la demande de moyens de defense a explose depuis les pillages. Jean-Pierre Bastie, president de l'Union francaise des amateurs d'armes, a declare a L'Est Republicain : « En region parisienne, les ventes ont ete multipliees par dix et les armuriers sont desormais en manque de materiel. » Les achats portent principalement sur les bombes lacrymogenes et les armes de defense non letales. Selon le premier bilan du ministre du Commerce Serge Papin, au moins 3 000 entreprises ont ete touchees par les violences des 17 et 18 octobre. La Ville de Paris activera le 24 octobre a midi une cellule de crise et prevoit des equipes supplementaires pour nettoyer les rues.

items.title: USA to host first women’s football Club World Cup in 2028 – FIFA
items.description: The United States will host the inaugural women’s football Club World Cup in 2028, FIFA announced Thursday. “The decision was taken in view of its experience in organising FIFA tournaments, the maturity of its infrastructure and services and the level of stakeholder interest in women’s football in the country,” world football’s governing body said. The competition will be staged from January 5-30, 2028. It will bring together 16 top-tier clubs from all six continental confederations. FIFA said the introduction of the tournament marked “a major milestone for the professionalisation and global expansion of the women’s club game, giving elite club sides a true world stage to compete on every four years”. Initially slated for 2026, FIFA pushed the inaugural tournament back by two years so it enjoys a clear window following the 2027 women’s World Cup and ahead of the 2028 Summer Olympics in Los Angeles. The US has a proven track record of hosting large sporting events, notably staging the men’s World Cup earlier this year. AFP The post USA to host first women’s football Club World Cup in 2028 – FIFA appeared first on Vanguard News .

items.title: France : quatre usines de Stellantis à l’arrêt, l’inquiétude monte pour 2027
items.description: Le constructeur automobile Stellantis (ex-Peugeot-Citroen) met temporairement a l'arret quatre de ses usines hexagonales, placant des milliers de salaries en chomage partiel et suscitant des interrogations sur l'avenir du secteur en France alors que le Mondial de l'auto a montre la crise europeenne en la matiere . a partir du 22 octobre, les usines de Sochaux (Doubs) et de Rennes (Ille-et-Vilaine) cessent leur activite jusqu'a la fin du mois. Le site de Mulhouse (Haut-Rhin) est deja a l'arret depuis mi-octobre, tandis que celui de Poissy (Yvelines) a interrompu son activite le 19 octobre. Au total, 8 400 salaries passent en chomage partiel et pres de 1 900 interimaires sont places en chomage technique. Stellantis met 8 400 salariés en chômage partiel dans quatre usines françaises parce que les batteries manquent l'assemblage final est en France, les ouvriers sont là, mais une seule pièce manque en amont et la production s'arrête les voitures électriques ont un seul composant qui bloque tout quand il manque, la batterie, et sa fabrication on l'a laissée se concentrer ailleurs pour de bonnes raisons à l'époque et plus tu pousses l'électrification, plus tu renforces une dépendance que tu n'as pas cherché à réduire avant la vraie question sur la souveraineté industrielle c'est quel maillon de la chaîne est concentré chez un seul fournisseur et impossible à remplacer rapidement si ça coupe — Léo Bachelot (@egocgp) October 19, 2026 a Sochaux, ou sont assemblees les Peugeot 3008 et 5008, et a Rennes, qui produit le Citroen C5 Aircross, les interruptions sont principalement dues a une penurie de batteries a grande autonomie fournies par Automotive Cells Company (ACC). Cette entreprise, detenue notamment par Stellantis, TotalEnergies et Mercedes-Benz, peine a satisfaire la demande, particulierement soutenue chez les clients professionnels. « On tourne vraiment au maximum de nos capacites actuelles », a reconnu le secretaire general d'ACC, Matthieu Hubert, aupres de BFMTV, le 19 octobre. Les interruptions doivent permettre de reconstituer les approvisionnements avant une reprise de la production debut novembre. a Mulhouse et a Poissy, les motifs sont differents. Les arrets visent principalement a reduire les stocks et a accompagner la fin du cycle de production de certains modeles, notamment les Peugeot 308 et 408 a Mulhouse. L'usine de Poissy doit, quant a elle, cesser l'assemblage automobile en 2027, avant sa reconversion en site de recyclage. Sur CNews, le 20 octobre, l'economiste Marc Touati a alerte sur les difficultes du constructeur, malgre la perspective du lancement d'une nouvelle 2CV : « Stellantis s'est effondree en bourse. » Marc Touati, économiste CNEWS : «Stellantis s’est effondrée en bourse», dans #LaMatinale Toute l'info est à retrouver sur https://t.co/NVs1Rf6rXd https://t.co/NVdv8BLNup — CNEWS (@CNEWS) October 20, 2026 De son cote, Fabien Roussel, candidat communiste a la presidentielle, a plaide pour la fabrication de cette nouvelle 2CV sur le territoire francais. Depuis le site de Poissy, dans les Yvelines, il a lance : « Produisons en France ces petits vehicules electriques avec les aides de l'etat, pour les rendre pas chers et creer plusieurs milliers d'emplois. » À Poissy, sur le site Stellantis, un seul mot d’ordre : la nouvelle 2CV doit être fabriquée ici ! Produisons en France ces petits véhicules électriques avec les aides de l’État, pour les rendre pas chers et créer plusieurs milliers d’emplois. L’argent public doit servir à ça ! https://t.co/VT3k3BFPES — Fabien Roussel (@Fabien_Roussel) October 15, 2026 Les aides publiques a l'industrie automobile francaise, vivement critiquees par la Cour des comptes, soulevent egalement des interrogations quant a leur compatibilite avec les regles europeennes. Chez Stellantis, les regards se tournent deja vers 2027. La direction doit presenter, fin octobre, ses previsions de production pour les trois prochaines annees. a Rennes, les syndicats redoutent la suppression d'une equipe si les volumes continuent de diminuer. a Mulhouse, la production pourrait fortement reculer dans l'attente de nouveaux modeles Peugeot. Sochaux semble mieux resister, mais sa direction craint qu'une partie de sa production ne soit transferee vers d'autres sites afin de mieux repartir la charge industrielle.

items.title: Speculations about Asiedu Nketia’s presidential bid deepen as he skips NDC chairmanship contest
items.description: The National Democratic Congress (NDC) has confirmed that its incumbent National Chairman, Johnson Asiedu Nketia, did not pick nomination forms to contest the party’s upcoming national executive elections. The party’s Director of Elections and IT, Mahdi Gibril, said Asiedu Nketiah, popularly known as “General Mosquito”, had not picked forms by the close of nominations and had not indicated an intention to contest. “These are those I know that did not pick. In any case, they did not indicate to us that they will pick,” Mr Gibril said. Although Asiedu Nketia has not formally declared a presidential bid, his decision not to seek another term as national chairman comes amid speculation about whether he intends to contest the NDC’s presidential primary ahead of the 2028 general elections. In August 2026, Asiedu Nketia was asked whether he had ruled out contesting the 2028 presidential election. He responded emphatically: “No, No, No!” “I have never ruled any position out in my life. I’m not ruling any position out,” he said at the time, listing the presidency among the positions he could consider. He also argued that ambition was essential in politics. “Ambition is a very useful thing in politics. If you are a politician and you have no ambition, you are in the wrong profession,” he said. His comments have continued to fuel speculation about his political plans, although he has not formally announced a presidential campaign. The NDC closed the picking of nomination forms for its 2026 National Executive Elections at 5 pm5pm on Wednesday, October 21. According to a statement signed by the Spokesperson for the Congress Elections Committee, Dr Peter Boamah Otokunor, a total of 137 prospective aspirants picked forms to contest 14 national executive positions. The figures include five aspirants for National Chairman, 19 for National Vice Chairman, two for General Secretary and 11 for Deputy General Secretary. With nominations closed, the process will move to the filing of completed forms, scheduled for November 7 to 9, ahead of the National Delegates Congress on December 19, 2026. Among the prominent figures linked to the National Chairman race is former chairman Samuel Ofosu-Ampofo, whose supporters purchased nomination forms on his behalf. Former Local Government Minister Akwasi Opong-Fosu, who declared his intention to contest in August 2026, and Ambassador Alhaji Said Sinare have also been associated with the race. Asiedu Nketiah has served as NDC National Chairman since December 2022, when he defeated Ofosu-Ampofo at the party’s 10th National Delegates Congress. His decision not to seek re-election leaves the chairmanship open as the party prepares to elect new national executives. The NDC’s national executive elections will determine the party’s leadership as it prepares for the 2028 general elections. The next stages include the filing of completed nomination forms and campaigning ahead of the December 19 congress. While Asiedu Nketiah’s decision not to contest the chairmanship has renewed attention on his political future, the party has not disclosed his reasons for opting out, and he has yet to formally declare a bid for the presidency.

items.title: Hardship: NLC, TUC give FG Oct 27 deadline, as talks deadlock
items.description: By Victor Ahiuma-Young ABUJA — The Nigeria Labour Congress (NLC) and the Trade Union Congress (TUC) have threatened possible nationwide action after talks with the Federal Government over workers’ welfare, petrol prices and other outstanding demands ended without a resolution. The meeting, held at the Ministry of Labour in Abuja on Thursday, October 22, ended in a deadlock, with organised labour giving the government until Tuesday, October 27, to make meaningful progress on the issues. The unions also directed their affiliates, state councils and civil society allies to begin mobilising members for possible nationwide action if the next round of talks fails to produce concrete commitments. In a joint statement signed by the NLC Acting General Secretary, Benson Upah, and the TUC Secretary-General, Nuhu Toro, the labour centres expressed disappointment with the government delegation’s preparedness for the meeting. The unions said their demands included a reduction in petrol prices to 2024 levels, renegotiation of the national minimum wage, implementation of agreed tax relief measures, fulfilment of the terms of settlement with the Joint Health Sector Unions (JOHESU), and resolution of demands by the Joint Public Service Negotiating Council (JPSNC) over peculiar allowance, wage award and hazard allowance. The statement said: “Regrettably, the government delegation came unprepared and without the necessary mandates to engage substantively on these issues. No concrete commitments were secured, and the outstanding issues remain unresolved.” According to the unions, the Minister of Labour requested that the meeting be adjourned until October 27 to allow the government to make adequate arrangements, including assembling relevant ministers and heads of departments and agencies. The labour centres said they remained committed to dialogue but warned that they would not accept indefinite delays in resolving the demands. The NLC said it would report the outcome of the meeting to its organs, adding that they would determine the next line of action if meaningful progress was not achieved at the next meeting. “We call on Nigerian workers and the general public to remain calm and resolute. Organised Labour will be attending the next meeting believing that government will deliver on each of the workers’ demands,” the statement said. The unions added that they would continue to pursue the interests of workers and the wider public through legitimate means. They also urged their affiliates, state councils and civil society allies to remain alert and begin preparations for possible nationwide action while awaiting the outcome of the next meeting. The unresolved demands cover issues affecting workers’ earnings and welfare, as well as wider concerns over the cost of living, including petrol prices, minimum wage negotiations, tax relief and outstanding allowances. The October 27 meeting is expected to provide another opportunity for the government and organised labour to address the outstanding issues. While the unions have maintained their commitment to dialogue, their mobilisation directive signals the possibility of an escalation if the next round of negotiations fails to produce meaningful progress. items.title: Algérie : la France aurait demandé davantage de pétrole et de GNL
items.description: La France aurait demande a l'Algerie d'augmenter « au plus vite » ses livraisons de petrole et de gaz naturel liquefie, rapporte le media specialise dans l'energie Attaqa , qui cite des sources proches du dossier, dans un article publie le 19 octobre. Selon cette publication, la demande francaise porterait sur une hausse urgente des approvisionnements afin de repondre aux besoins energetiques du pays. Aucun volume supplementaire ni calendrier de livraison n'a toutefois ete communique publiquement. Le ministere algerien de l'energie n'avait pas repondu aux sollicitations du media au moment de la parution de l'article. Cette demarche presumee survient alors que les marches europeens de l'energie restent soumis a des tensions, sur fond de conflit au Moyen-Orient. L'approche de la periode hivernale, marquee par une hausse habituelle de la consommation de gaz, renforce les enjeux de securite d'approvisionnement. La proximite geographique de l'Algerie constitue un atout pour les livraisons vers la France, notamment par rapport aux importations en provenance de regions exposees a des perturbations du transport maritime. Alger figure parmi les fournisseurs de gaz et de petrole du marche europeen. Des capacites soumises aux engagements contractuels Selon Attaqa , les exportations de petrole algerien vers la France auraient atteint environ 138 000 barils par jour en avril 2026, contre 43 000 en mars. Cette progression ne suffit pas a etablir que l'Algerie dispose de volumes supplementaires immediatement disponibles pour repondre a une nouvelle demande francaise. La capacite d'Alger a accroître ses livraisons dependrait notamment des discussions entre les deux parties, des possibilites de production et d'exportation de Sonatrach, la compagnie nationale algerienne, ainsi que de ses engagements contractuels envers d'autres clients. Le gaz naturel liquefie est particulierement concerne par ces contraintes. Une eventuelle hausse des livraisons a la France devrait tenir compte des contrats deja conclus avec d'autres partenaires, en particulier europeens. L'Algerie a en effet renforce ses relations energetiques avec plusieurs pays du continent depuis la reduction des livraisons russes. L'Europe cherche a securiser ses approvisionnements La France ne serait pas le seul pays europeen a s'interesser davantage au gaz et au petrole algeriens. L'Allemagne, l'Italie et l'Espagne ont aussi multiplie les echanges avec Alger autour de la cooperation energetique. L'Italie a ainsi place la question du gaz au cœur de ses discussions avec les autorites algeriennes lors de la visite de la Premiere ministre italienne Giorgia Meloni en mars 2026. L'Allemagne cherche, de son cote, a diversifier ses sources d'approvisionnement, tandis que l'Espagne entretient des relations energetiques etroites avec l'Algerie. Ces sollicitations s'inscrivent dans un contexte de concurrence entre acheteurs pour l'acces au gaz. La capacite de l'Algerie a repondre a d'eventuelles demandes supplementaires dependra neanmoins de ses disponibilites et de ses engagements commerciaux existants. Des relations politiques toujours delicates La demande francaise rapportee par Attaqa survient alors que les relations entre Paris et Alger restent marquees par des differends diplomatiques, notamment sur le Sahara occidental, l'immigration, la securite et la memoire de la colonisation. Le president francais Emmanuel Macron s'est aussi rendu dans quatre pays du Golfe, du 19 au 21 octobre, pour discuter de l'approvisionnement energetique et de la hausse des prix des carburants. a ce stade, aucune confirmation officielle de la demande francaise ni aucun accord portant sur des volumes supplementaires n'ont ete rendus publics. Les eventuelles consequences de cette demarche sur l'approvisionnement de la France dependront donc des discussions entre Paris et Alger et des capacites de livraison de Sonatrach.

items.title: Deux failles majeures provoquent des millions de tentatives de cyberattaque dans le monde
items.description: Des la divulgation, le 21 octobre, de deux vulnerabilites majeures affectant PHP, les tentatives d'exploitation se sont multipliees. Ce langage de programmation est utilise par de nombreux sites internet, exposant potentiellement un grand nombre de serveurs. Les administrateurs ont dû deployer rapidement des mises a jour de securite pour empecher l'exploitation de ces failles. Cloudflare, dont les systemes protegent de nombreux sites internet, a observe l'explosion du nombre de tentatives. Son directeur general, Matthew Prince, a raconte sur X, le 21 octobre, la vitesse a laquelle les attaques avaient progresse. « Dans les dix heures precedant l'annonce publique, nous avons observe sur l'ensemble de notre reseau des milliers de tentatives d'exploitation. Ce chiffre est passe a des dizaines de milliers dans les 45 minutes suivant l'annonce, a des centaines de milliers en deux heures et se compte desormais en millions. » Ces vulnerabilites existaient depuis plusieurs annees dans PHP. Elles ont ete reperees avec l'aide de l'intelligence artificielle et permettent, lorsqu'elles sont exploitees, d'acceder a certaines donnees ou d'executer du code sur un serveur. Les versions corrigees ont ete publiees le 21 octobre. Des services bancaires, administratifs et de transport suspendus Au Japon, Mitsubishi UFJ, la compagnie aerienne ANA et East Japan Railway ont suspendu une partie de leurs services en ligne. Meme precaution dans plusieurs administrations. Pour les utilisateurs, les interruptions ont ete immediates, alors que les equipes techniques s'efforcaient de mettre les systemes a jour. Le groupe francais Orange a suspendu l'acces a certains sites et applications utilisant PHP dans plusieurs de ses filiales, sans preciser tous les services concernes. a Paris, la mairie a egalement place plusieurs sites municipaux en maintenance pour installer les correctifs. En Finlande, des services publics ont commence a rouvrir apres leur mise a jour. La Chine a demande aux organisations de verifier leurs installations et la Coree du Sud a releve son niveau d'alerte pour le secteur prive. Les millions de tentatives signalees par Cloudflare ne representent pas autant de piratages reussis. Mais les correctifs ne suffisent pas toujours a rouvrir un service immediatement. Certains systemes doivent encore etre testes et les plus anciens necessitent des modifications plus importantes. En Finlande, l'operateur public Valtori previent que le retour a la normale peut prendre plusieurs jours, voire plusieurs semaines.

items.title: 10 items you cannot bring along with you on your trip to the UK
items.description: Travellers heading to the United Kingdom must be careful about the items they pack, as UK border authorities prohibit or restrict certain goods to protect public safety, human health, animals and the environment. The UK government has rules covering controlled drugs, weapons, certain food products, counterfeit goods and items made from endangered species. Some goods may be confiscated at the border, while carrying prohibited items can lead to fines or prosecution. According to the UK government’s official guidance on banned and restricted goods, travellers should check the applicable rules before departure. Here are 10 items travellers should avoid packing for a trip to the UK unless they have confirmed that the items are permitted under the relevant rules. 1. Illegal drugs Travellers cannot bring controlled drugs such as cocaine, heroin, MDMA, cannabis and methamphetamine into the UK without the authorisation required under applicable law. Some medicines containing controlled substances may be permitted under specific conditions, but travellers should not assume that a prescription automatically authorises them to carry every controlled drug across the border. Those travelling with prescribed medication should check the UK government’s guidance on bringing medicines into the UK. 2. Prohibited knives and offensive weapons Certain knives and weapons are banned from importation into the UK. These include flick knives, butterfly knives, disguised knives, knuckledusters, push daggers and some types of swords. Other prohibited or restricted weapons include stun guns, self-defence sprays and certain martial arts weapons. Travellers should not pack these items for personal protection or as souvenirs without first checking the applicable rules. Some weapons may be imported only under specific exemptions or with the required authorisation. The UK government provides further details in its guidance on guns, knives, swords and other offensive weapons. 3. Pepper spray and CS gas Pepper spray and CS gas are prohibited from being brought into the UK as ordinary personal belongings. Although some travellers may carry these products for self-defence in their home countries, UK rules classify them as prohibited weapons. Travellers should therefore avoid packing pepper spray, CS gas canisters and similar self-defence sprays in either their hand luggage or checked baggage. 4. Meat and meat products from Nigeria Travellers coming from Nigeria and other countries outside the relevant permitted categories generally cannot bring meat or meat products into Great Britain for personal consumption. This includes products such as beef, goat meat, poultry, sausages and other foods containing prohibited meat products. The restriction means travellers should not assume that cooked, dried, smoked or packaged meat is automatically allowed through customs. Nigerians travelling with local delicacies should check the ingredients carefully before packing them. The UK government’s guidance on bringing meat, dairy, fish and other animal products into Great Britain explains the applicable restrictions and exceptions. 5. Milk and dairy products Milk, cheese, butter, yoghurt and other dairy products are subject to restrictions when brought into Great Britain from abroad. For travellers arriving from Nigeria, milk and milk-based products are generally prohibited, although exceptions exist for certain products, including specified infant formula and special foods required for medical reasons. The rules include conditions on quantities and packaging for eligible exceptions. Travellers should check the latest requirements before carrying powdered milk, cheese, butter or other dairy products in their luggage. 6. Endangered animal and plant products Items made from endangered animals or plants may be prohibited or require special permits and certificates before they can enter the UK. These can include ivory ornaments, certain animal skins, exotic leather products, protected coral, rare plants and souvenirs made from endangered species. Some products may appear to be ordinary gifts or decorative items but still fall under international wildlife-trade restrictions. Travellers should not assume that buying an item legally in another country means they can bring it into the UK without documentation. The UK government advises travellers to check whether they need a CITES permit for protected species. 7. Counterfeit designer goods and pirated products Counterfeit goods and pirated products may be seized by UK authorities, and travellers could face legal consequences depending on the circumstances. Examples include fake designer handbags, imitation branded shoes, counterfeit clothing, pirated films and unauthorised copies of copyrighted products. The rules can apply even when the items are purchased abroad and packed as gifts or personal belongings. Travellers should avoid carrying counterfeit products and should check the relevant customs rules before bringing branded goods into the country. 8. Indecent or prohibited obscene material Certain indecent or obscene materials are prohibited from entering the UK. These can include publications, films, videos, photographs and other material that falls within the relevant legal restrictions. Material involving child sexual abuse is particularly serious and may constitute a criminal offence. Travellers should not assume that material legally available in another country can automatically be imported into the UK. The restrictions may also apply to prohibited material stored on electronic devices or other media. 9. Firearms, ammunition and explosives without the required authorisation Firearms, ammunition and explosives are subject to strict import controls. Travellers cannot simply pack them in their luggage and enter the UK without meeting the relevant legal requirements. Depending on the item, travellers may need an import licence, firearms certificate or other official permission. The rules also cover certain realistic imitation firearms and restricted weapons. People travelling for sporting competitions, historical events or other authorised purposes should confirm the requirements well before departure. The UK government’s weapons import guidance provides further information. 10. Rough diamonds and certain protected natural materials Rough diamonds are among the goods prohibited from entering the UK unless the applicable requirements are met. Other natural materials, including products derived from protected wildlife, may also be subject to strict controls or require permits. Travellers carrying valuable stones, wildlife souvenirs or unusual natural products should verify their legal status before packing them. The UK government’s list of banned and restricted goods explains the relevant restrictions. Before travelling, passengers should also remember that not every item subject to customs rules is completely banned. Some food products, plants, medicines and valuable goods may be permitted if the traveller meets the applicable conditions or obtains the required documentation. The rules can differ between Great Britain and Northern Ireland, as well as according to the country from which the traveller is arriving. Travellers should consult the official UK government guidance on bringing goods into the country before departure to avoid having their belongings confiscated or facing possible legal penalties. Vanguard News The post 10 items you cannot bring along with you on your trip to the UK appeared first on Vanguard News .
