items.title: Ébola en RDC : le flou financier fragilise la riposte
items.description: © Internet La plus grave épidémie d’Ébola en République démocratique du Congo a franchi les frontières du pays. Alors que le bilan dépasse 4 500 morts, Africa CDC réclame des explications sur plus de 700 millions de dollars dont l’utilisation est difficile à retracer. Déclarée en mai dans l’Ituri, l’épidémie provoquée par le virus Bundibugyo continue de s’étendre malgré les moyens internationaux mobilisés. Selon les données arrêtées au 17 octobre, la RDC comptait 9 455 cas confirmés et 4 561 décès. Le virus touchait 66 zones de santé dans huit provinces, le Nord-Ubangi étant la dernière atteinte. Plus de 900 malades étaient hospitalisés en isolement. Le passage du virus au Kenya a donné une dimension régionale à la crise. Le premier malade, arrivé de RDC par l’Ouganda, est décédé le 5 octobre à Nairobi. Sept autres contaminations ont ensuite été détectées parmi ses proches, des soignants et un accompagnant hospitalier. Toutes sont liées à ce premier cas et les autorités kenyanes n’ont pas signalé de transmission communautaire. Nairobi a renforcé les contrôles aux frontières, tandis que la Tanzanie surveille pendant 21 jours les voyageurs venant des pays à risque. Plus de 700 millions de dollars à tracer La progression de l’épidémie s’accompagne d’une controverse sur le financement de la riposte. Selon le Directeur général d’Africa CDC, Jean Kaseya, les bailleurs déclarent avoir versé 962 millions de dollars aux organisations chargées des interventions. Mais une vérification menée avec les autorités congolaises n’aurait permis de documenter précisément qu’un peu plus de 200 millions. Plus de 700 millions de dollars restent ainsi insuffisamment renseignés dans les rapports financiers disponibles. Ce constat ne prouve pas un détournement. Il révèle toutefois un sérieux déficit de transparence entre bailleurs, organisations internationales, ONG et autorités nationales. Le gouvernement congolais affirme ne pas avoir reçu directement ces fonds et a limité à 25 le nombre d’ONG autorisées à intervenir, sur près d’une centaine précédemment présentes. Cette opacité devient aussi un problème sanitaire. Des agents mobilisés en première ligne ont protesté contre des retards de paiement et des conditions de travail difficiles. Dans des régions marquées par les violences armées et la méfiance envers les institutions, les zones d’ombre financières fragilisent la confiance des communautés. Publier les montants reçus, les dépenses et leurs bénéficiaires apparaît aussi nécessaire que renforcer le dépistage, l’isolement et le suivi des contacts. D’où l’urgence de faire toute la lumière sur cette affaire.

items.title: Sustain economic stability, expand productive employment and create better jobs – ISSER to government
items.description: The Institute of Statistical, Social and Economic Research (ISSER) wants government to sustain the economic stability while expanding productive employment, saying it will be critical to translating economic growth into improved living standards. In its State of Ghana Economic Report (SGER), ISSER said Ghana’s macroeconomic recovery gained momentum in 2025, but growth remained uneven across sector. Ghana’s economy grew by 6.0% in 2025, up from 5.8% in 2024 and above the global (3.4%) and sub-Saharan African (4.5%) averages. Growth was driven mainly by services (8.1%) and agriculture (6.8%). Industry slowed to 2.3%, largely reflecting a sharp contraction in oil and gas production, although manufacturing and gold production expanded. The macroeconomic conditions also improved considerably. Year-end inflation fell from 23.8% to 5.4%, the cedi strengthened, and interest rates declined. The fiscal deficit narrowed, while strong gold exports contributed to a substantial improvement in the external position and international reserves. ISSER said a lower inflation and a stronger currency provide relief to households and businesses, while improved fiscal and external conditions create a more favourable environment for investment. However, the stronger Gross Domestic Product (GDP) growth does not automatically translate into better livelihoods. “Employment opportunities, the cost of borrowing and the distribution of growth benefits remain important concerns”, it argued. Policy Priorities In sustaining stability, ISSER urged the government to maintain fiscal discipline and low inflation while supporting productive investment. It also wants the government to creating better jobs whilst translate growth into employment opportunities, particularly for young people. Again, it called for strengthening resilience, saying, diversify production and exports, improve infrastructure and reduce dependence on commodity-driven gains.

items.title: President Zardari departs for Germany on 3-day visit to discuss bilateral ties
items.description: President Asif Ali Zardari departed for Germany on Thursday on a three-day visit to discuss bilateral ties as the two countries are set to mark the 75th anniversary of their diplomatic relations. In a statement issued earlier, the Foreign Office (FO) said the president’s visit, scheduled for Oct 22-24, is “part of high-level exchanges between Pakistan and Germany”. President Zardari “has departed from Lahore for Germany”, the President’s office said on social media on Thursday. The FO statement highlighted that the visit “holds special significance in the context of the 75th anniversary of the establishment of diplomatic relations between the two countries being commemorated this year”. It said the visit reflects the “deep commitment of both countries to further strengthening the partnership”. During his visit, President Zardari will hold meetings with his German counterpart Frank-Walter Steinmeier, as well as senior leadership and business leaders, with a “particular focus оп economic and trade cooperation”, FO said. Sindh Chief Minister Murad Ali Shah is also expected to accompany the president on his trip, with the matter being discussed in Murad’s meeting with German Consul General Thomas E. Schultze. In September, Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar met German Foreign Minister Johann Wadephul on the sidelines of the United Nations General Assembly. During the meeting, Germany appreciated Pakistan’s mediation efforts in regional conflicts, especially in the Strait of Hormuz and Bab al-Mandab while the two sides also agreed to “get negotiations on peace for Ukraine going”, according to the German foreign office. Meanwhile, in June, a German delegation announced plans to bring about 30 German companies to Pakistan and link local businesses to European markets.

items.title: Pakistan, EU agree to strengthen counterterrorism cooperation at multilateral forums
items.description: Pakistan and the European Union (EU) have agreed to strengthen cooperation at multilateral forums, including the United Nations, to advance a coherent counterterrorism approach, according to a statement issued by the Foreign Office (FO) on Thursday. The agreement was reached during the 10th round of the Pakistan-EU Bilateral Counterterrorism Dialogue, held in Islamabad. The Pakistani delegation was led by Dr Fareha Bugti, director general (counterterrorism), while the EU side was headed by Anna Strazska, the European External Action Service’s special envoy for counterterrorism. During the meeting, the two sides exchanged views on recent regional and global developments affecting the terrorism threat landscape and unequivocally condemned terrorism in all its forms, reaffirming their commitment to combating the threat. According to FO, the EU condemned recent terrorist attacks in Pakistan, expressed solidarity with the suffering of affected civilians and recognised the value of Pakistan’s efforts to combat terrorism. “Acknowledging each other’s role in the ongoing global fight against terrorism, Pakistan and the EU expressed concern at the security implications of the situation in Afghanistan,” the statement added. The two sides maintained that effective multilateralism remained essential to building lasting international consensus on terrorism. The discussions also addressed the evolving nature of terrorist threats, including the exploitation of cyberspace and information and energy resources to advance their objectives, the statement said. The FO said Pakistan and the EU exchanged best practices on preventing and countering violent extremism, terrorism financing and radicalisation in all forms, particularly the use of cyberspace by terrorists. It added that the “two sides identified priority areas for cooperation and reaffirmed their commitment to regular, institutionalised engagement on counterterrorism”. The FO said the next round of the dialogue would be held in Brussels at a mutually convenient date next year. The dialogue comes as Pakistan’s counterterrorism challenge enters a new and more complex phase, with terrorist groups evolving their methods of financing and recruitment. On Tuesday, an international seminar on Pakistan’s evolving counterterrorism landscape, organised by the Institute of Strategic Studies Islamabad, highlighted the changing methods of terrorist groups, including their financing and recruitment. Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar urged the Afghan authorities to take “concrete, verifiable and irreversible action” against the banned Tehreek-i-Taliban Pakistan (TTP) and other groups operating from Afghan soil. Information Minister Attaullah Tarar, who also addressed the seminar, cited UN assessments indicating that more than 6,000 TTP fighters were present in Afghanistan, with the overall militant presence exceeding 20,000.

items.title: 65 inspecteurs du Trésor, 36 inspecteurs des Impôts, 20 contrôleurs : une promotion gabonaise sans échec au Burkina Faso
items.description: Libreville a célébré, ce mercredi 21 octobre, l’excellence au service des Finances publiques. Les directions générales du Trésor public et des Impôts ont organisé, sous l’égide des ministères de l’Économie et des Finances et de la Fonction publique, la remise des diplômes aux 121 lauréats de la 36 e promotion, 2 e cohorte 2026, de l’Institut des finances publiques du Burkina Faso (IFPB). Ayant reçu leurs parchemins, les 65 inspecteurs centraux du Trésor, 36 inspecteurs centraux des Impôts et 20 contrôleurs des Impôts, ont eu une consigne du ministère de l’Économie et des Finances : transformer leurs connaissances en « résultats tangibles pour la collectivité nationale ». Les nouveaux diplômés immortalisés avec les représentants des différentes administrations et de l’IFPB, à l’issue de la remise des diplômes aux Gabonais, lauréats de l’IFPB, le 21 octobre 2026, à Libreville. © GabonReview 121 ! Tel est le nombre de cadres gabonais, formés et dorénavant diplômés de l’Institut des finances publiques du Burkina Faso (IFPB) qui ont reçu, ce mercredi 21 octobre, à Libreville leur diplôme. Ce qui a davantage fortifié la coopération bilatérale entre le Gabon et le Burkina Faso notamment dans le renforcement des compétences de l’administration financière. Dans ce sens, la cérémonie de remise des diplômes aux lauréats de la 36ᵉ promotion, 2ᵉ cohorte 2026, de cet Institut, a été organisée à l’initiative des directions générales du Trésor public et des Impôts, sous la tutelle des ministères de l’Économie et des Finances et de la Fonction publique. Transformer les connaissances acquises en compétences opérationnelles Quelques moments de la remise des diplômes aux Gabonais, lauréats de l’IFPB, le 21 octobre 2026, à Libreville. © GabonReview Représentant le ministre de l’Économie et des Finances, le Secrétaire général Michel Tsamba a salué une promotion « remarquable », marquée par un taux de réussite de 100% et des moyennes comprises entre 12 et 17 sur 20. Des résultats qui traduisent l’assiduité des stagiaires et la qualité de l’encadrement, mais qui doivent se traduire aussi par des résultats tangibles au sein des administrations auxquelles ils sont destinés. « Il vous appartient désormais de transformer les connaissances acquises en compétences opérationnelles, les compétences en performances mesurables et les performances en résultats tangibles pour la collectivité nationale», a-t-il conseillé, insistant également sur l’intégrité et le rejet de la corruption. «Vous étiez auditeurs maintenant, vous êtes des ambassadeurs» Il a par ailleurs fait noter que chaque « recette correctement recouvrée, chaque opération fidèlement comptabilisée et chaque contrôle conduit avec discernement protège les ressources nécessaires aux services publics et au développement ». Pour lui, « la qualité de nos finances publiques dépend d’abord des femmes et des hommes qui les servent ». Au total, 121 agents ont donc bénéficié de ce programme, au terme de 24 mois de formation ponctués de soutenances. La cohorte comprend 65 inspecteurs centraux du Trésor, 36 inspecteurs centraux des Impôts et 20 contrôleurs des Impôts. Et la représentante des récipiendaires, Rose Ntémé, a, pour sa part, exprimé leur disponibilité à mettre leurs acquis au service du pays, avec rigueur et transparence. De son côté, le directeur général de l’IFPB, Barthélémy Dabré, qui a fait le déplacement de Libreville, a résumé leur nouvelle responsabilité, déclarant que « vous étiez auditeurs maintenant, vous êtes des ambassadeurs » et les engageant à être exemplaires de l’Institut, de l’encadrement et des formations reçues. Que cet investissement dans la formation se traduise par une gestion plus fiable, transparente ! Cette cérémonie a témoigné de la portée d’un partenariat conclu le 4 octobre 2024 et inscrit dans lignée une coopération ancienne avec le Burkina FGaso, qui a déjà contribué à former plusieurs cadres gabonais, notamment Luther Abouna Yangui, l’actuel directeur général de la Comptabilité publique et du Trésor, Éric Boumah, ancien directeur général des Impôts et le général de brigade Hugues Modeste Odjangou, premier responsables des Douanes gabonaise. Pour les deux pays, cette collaboration Sud-Sud constitue un outil de partage d’expertise et de consolidation de la collaboration entre les administrations financières. Le défi est désormais de permettre aux nouveaux diplômés d’exercer effectivement leurs compétences, afin que cet investissement dans la formation se traduise par une gestion plus fiable, transparente et efficace des deniers publics. Ce, d’autant plus que ces nouveaux inspecteurs et contrôleurs sont appelés à renforcer la gouvernance, la transparence et la gestion des ressources publiques de l’État gabonais, à condition que les administrations assurent rapidement leur affectation, leurs moyens et un suivi de leurs progrès. L’article 65 inspecteurs du Trésor, 36 inspecteurs des Impôts, 20 contrôleurs : une promotion gabonaise sans échec au Burkina Faso est apparu en premier sur Gabonreview.com | Actualité du Gabon | .

items.title: America Is About to See What Happens When Voters Turn to AI
items.description: If you were wondering whether AI could make the midterms even more confusing, here’s one data point: Several people who thought they were donating to James Talarico unwittingly gave their money to someone else. Talarico, a Texas Democrat, is running for Senate in what’s probably the most closely watched race of the upcoming elections. Search Google for how to contribute to his campaign, and you might get an AI-generated answer that links to ways “you can chip in securely.” Until a few weeks ago, one of those featured links was actually controlled by an unrelated political-action committee that sent the money instead to the reelection campaign of another Democrat: Senator John Hickenlooper of Colorado. The mix-up wasn’t all AI’s fault. The link led to a misleading donation page that carried Talarico’s name and picture, and specified only at the bottom that the money would go to Hickenlooper. But Google’s AI tool evidently didn’t read the fine print. And perhaps no one would have clicked on it had Google not highlighted the page in an authoritative-sounding AI response. A spokesperson for Hickenlooper’s campaign told me that the Colorado Democrat, whose seat is considered safe, had not intentionally siphoned the donations. Rather, an outside group, the Kitchen Table Values PAC, had created the fundraiser without Hickenlooper’s knowledge. This appears to have fooled at least three people, who donated a combined total of $1,011, the spokesperson said. Rich Wilkins, the Democratic organizer behind the PAC, told me that the money was supposed to be split between Talarico and his group. “If a page was incorrectly going to Hickenlooper, that sounds like a human-error issue,” he said. After a Democratic digital-advertising strategist discovered the misleading fundraiser while Googling his party’s Senate candidates, the page was removed from the fundraising platform ActBlue, and Hickenlooper’s campaign forwarded the misdirected money to Talarico. The 2026 midterms will mark the first federal election in which tens of millions of voters are getting some of their political information from generative-AI tools. In a September survey, the American Association of Political Consultants Foundation reported that 4 percent of respondents had consulted a chatbot such as ChatGPT for election information in the previous month. Far more—nearly 40 percent—reported getting such info from Google’s AI-search summaries. As the election nears, those numbers will surely rise. There’s a reason for AI’s growing popularity with voters: These tools are convenient, and their answers are personalized. In theory, they have the potential to debunk the kinds of corrosive conspiracy theories that flourish on social media; even Grok, Elon Musk’s chatbot, will correctly tell you that Donald Trump lost the 2020 election. But chatbots are already bringing new complications to an internet that has been teeming with political falsehoods and distortions. Between fake-news sites cropping up to influence AI answers, models that are drawing on foreign propaganda, and chatbots dispensing misleading voter information, the age of AI-mediated politics is beginning to feel awfully familiar. [ Read: What Trump’s chatbot told me about the election ] In the lead-up to the 2024 presidential election, most chatbots couldn’t search the web, and they were trained to tread cautiously around questions about elections and current events. Today’s AI tools are still instructed not to take sides politically, but they’ve evolved into all-purpose assistants that will answer your election questions directly, confidently—and sometimes wrongly. In a forthcoming report, Forum AI, a start-up that evaluates AI models’ performance on questions about controversial topics, found that about 40 percent of chatbots’ answers to election-related questions contained at least one factual inaccuracy. When Forum’s researchers asked one widely used model when they needed to request a mail-in ballot to vote in the midterms in Pennsylvania, the chatbot said November 3. The actual deadline is a week earlier. (Forum did not specify the precise AI model.) In the same report , shared with The Atlantic ahead of its publication, Forum determined that about one in three responses cited an unreliable information source, such as posts on Reddit or Quora. Google’s Gemini answered a question about why America’s global power is declining by citing an article from People’s Daily , a Chinese state-run news outlet. “These aren’t trick questions,” Campbell Brown, a co-founder of Forum AI, told me. “There’s no excuse for chatbots to keep getting them wrong.” The companies say their bots have improved since Forum conducted its research in August. Over the past two months, Google, OpenAI, and Anthropic have all partnered with the nonpartisan nonprofit Democracy Works to pull accurate, up-to-date information about how, where, and when to vote. OpenAI’s GPT-5.6 was the most accurate of the models tested by Forum, and Nate Evans, a spokesperson for OpenAI, told me he believes that the company’s bots should rate higher now. In an email, the Google spokesperson Davis Thompson told me that the company tests its AI answers on election topics “extensively,” and that these responses show up on Google searches only when the company is confident AI can provide good information. A spokesperson for Anthropic, whose integration with Democracy Works launched last week, declined to comment. Chatbots can be uniquely convincing. In a recent report from the Brennan Center for Justice, a nonpartisan think tank, a researcher posed as a Dallas-area real-estate agent who was suspicious of the election process. Claude responded that the feeling of disempowerment was “completely understandable” but insisted that elections aren’t actually run by a “shadowy group of elites” in Washington. The problem is, most people don’t particularly want to be talked out of their beliefs, Gideon Nave, a professor at the University of Pennsylvania’s Wharton School of Business who studies AI and cognition, told me. He worries that the same persuasive power that can convince a conspiracy theorist that the moon landing was real could also make AI a potent tool for manipulation of public opinion. “You can implant all sorts of ideas in people’s heads when they’re using AI, and they feel that it’s their own responses.” Inevitably, a cottage industry has sprung up to consult candidates on how to influence what AI says about them. On the left, the advocacy group Run for Something launched a platform called CampSight that monitors what LLMs are saying about an issue or candidate and recommends how to shape those narratives. On the right, the Center for Campaign Innovation has published research on how AI models respond to questions about candidates and the sources they most often cite. “We’re campaigning for the AI vote now,” Eric Wilson, the group’s director, told me. Some of the most effective “sloptimization” tactics are simple, though not always obvious. “Most candidates we talked to were not filling out Ballotpedia profiles,” Jordan Haines, Run for Something’s chief technology officer, told me, referring to the online repository of election information. “They were like, ‘Eh, no one really reads that.’” Most voters may not be visiting Ballotpedia in droves, but it turns out that their chatbots are. LLMs also love websites with dot-gov domains, both Haines and Wilson told me. That could lend an advantage to incumbents, who can use their official House.gov or Senate.gov web pages to seed messaging for chatbots to pick up on. Challengers, though, might find AI answers easier to sway, because there’s often less information about them in the public record. [ Read: Your search results are getting sloptimized ] Official government websites typically don’t draw contrast between candidates or weigh the relative merits of differing views. Yet those are the kinds of questions people are starting to ask AI. To answer them, chatbots can’t always turn to mainstream news outlets; many have put up measures that block AI bots from ingesting their articles without a specific content agreement. ( The Atlantic, for instance, has a corporate content-licensing deal with OpenAI, and otherwise blocks most AI crawlers.) Good sources can be especially scarce for state and local races, Katie Harbath, whose firm, Anchor Change, advises tech companies on policy, told me. To fill those gaps, AI tools may scrounge among iffy sources. Researchers at a cybersecurity start-up called VisionHeight told me that they recently discovered 37 different suspicious websites, all registered on the same night in September, that seem tailor-made to appear in AI answers about elections. The sites carry newspapery names such as the Scranton Beacon and the Tar Heel State Report, but they read nothing like newspapers. Instead they are stuffed with questions and answers about state and local candidates. “Which candidate in MI-04 has the stronger plan for public safety?” asks one page on the Wolverine State Report. Its answer begins: “Sean McCann is the stronger choice,” referring to the Democratic nominee for Congress from that district. At least some of this material is already making its way into AI answers. When I asked Google’s Gemini-powered “AI Mode” Does Sean McCann support defunding the police? , its response drew on and cited the Wolverine State Report and the Kalamazoo Beacon, both of which are part of the network that VisionHeight discovered. The answer in this case was not necessarily inaccurate; his campaign website says he doesn’t. (McCann is just one of many candidates named by the Wolverine State Report, and there’s no reason to believe he had anything to do with the website. His campaign did not not respond to a request for comment.) Thompson, the Google spokesperson, said that “data voids” are long-standing problems for search engines and AI answers alike, and that the company is always looking out for coordinated attempts to exploit them. After I asked him about the network of sites, the sources seemed to stop appearing in search results. And Google’s AI Mode began giving a different answer about McCann’s position: Whether he supports defunding the police “depends on the perspectives of his campaign and his political opponents,” it said. Although it’s unclear who is behind the network of midterm-focused sites, trolls and foreign governments could use similar methods to seed lies for chatbots to regurgitate. According to the Global Disinformation Index, chatbots have already cited a false claim by the Russian defense ministry to wrongly answer a question about Russia’s control of Ukraine. And on Wednesday, NewsGuard, a company that tracks misinformation, reported that Google’s AI answers had picked up on a deepfake video spread by a Russian influence campaign that falsely depicts a student accusing Talarico of sexual assault in 2012. A decade ago, the 2016 election revealed how social media had corroded the political-information sphere. The last thing AI companies want is another Cambridge Analytica : They are rolling out blog posts cataloging their preparations against misinformation and manipulation. “We take the responsibility to deliver high quality, trustworthy information seriously,” Google says, a claim echoed by OpenAI and Anthropic. It’s reassuring that they say they’re taking that responsibility seriously. It just happens to be the same thing the social-media companies have been telling us for years. Victoria Feng contributed reporting.

items.title: Faster reforms could triple Pakistan’s incomes by 2050, says World Bank
items.description: ISLAMABAD: Pakistan’s incomes could triple by 2050 if the country ensures faster implementation of structural reforms, according to the World Bank Group’s latest Pakistan Development Update, titled Attaining Escape Velocity. The report says that following progress on macroeconomic stabilisation, Pakistan has an opportunity to achieve faster and sustained economic growth and create more jobs. Sound macroeconomic policies in recent years have helped stabilise the economy and preserve growth despite the impact of the Middle East conflict . Real gross domestic product (GDP) growth increased to 3.7 per cent in FY26 from 3.2pc in FY25. Revenue growth and expenditure restraint supported record primary fiscal surpluses, which reached 2.9pc of GDP in FY26, while strong remittances enabled the country to rebuild its foreign exchange reserves. These improvements were recognised through upgrades by two major international rating agencies, S&P and Moody’s , and enabled Pakistan to return to international debt markets with the issuance of a $3 billion Eurobond. “Pakistan has made real progress in restoring stability, and markets have taken notice,” World Bank Country Dir­ector Bolormaa Amgaa­baz­­ar said. “But real per capita growth — the rate at which the income of the average Pakistani increases — remains stuck at around 1.6pc. Reforms to drive faster growth are now urgently needed,” she added. The report finds that higher growth is possible if Pakistan follows the path taken by other successful countries in pursuing ambitious economic reforms. Upgrading policies and institutions to the standards of the average middle-income country could drive sustained annual growth of 6.2pc to 6.9pc, allowing Pakistan to reach Vietnam’s current income level by 2050. “With macro stabilisation achieved but fiscal resources and foreign exchange still tightly constrained, structural reform to encourage private investment is the necessary next step towards higher living standards,” said Sebastian Essl, the report’s lead author. “Achieving this kind of private-sector-led growth requires a plan, coordination, and committed reform implementation,” he added. The report outlines an ambitious set of reforms that could enable Pakistan to attain by 2050 the per capita income levels of countries currently at the upper-middle-income threshold. Many of the proposed measures build on reforms already underway. These include timely adjustments to power-sector tariffs, which helped reduce energy subsidies from 1.1pc of GDP in FY25 to 0.8pc in FY26, continued trade liberalisation under the National Tariff Policy and the recent privatisation of Pakistan International Airlines (PIA). Building on these measures, sustained progress will depend on further reforms to improve the business environment, overhaul the tax system, reduce the state’s presence in the economy and expand access to finance.

items.title: NBA : Mouhamed Gueye vise un retour fin novembre après sa fracture au pied
items.description: Les Atlanta Hawks devront encore patienter avant de retrouver Mouhamed Gueye. L'intérieur sénégalais, absent depuis le début de la saison, pourrait refouler les parquets autour du 20 novembre 2026. Tout remonte au 8 juillet dernier. À l'entraînement, le joueur de 23 ans s'est fracturé le pied gauche. Il a été opéré le 14 juillet à Atlanta, et depuis, la franchise de Géorgie suit de près l'évolution de sa convalescence. Cette échéance de fin novembre n'est cependant qu'une estimation : elle doit encore être confirmée officiellement par le club. Gueye avait pourtant bien compté la saison passée dans la rotation des Hawks. Il avait pris part à 77 rencontres, pour 4,4 points et 3,6 rebonds de moyenne en 15,3 minutes par match. Le Sénégalais poursuit aujourd'hui sa rééducation, avec l'espoir d'être de retour avant la fin du mois de novembre. Son calendrier dépendra toutefois de l'évolution de sa condition physique et de la décision du staff médical d'Atlanta. O.B.N

items.title: Marché de Matoto : Mohamed Soumah entendu au commissariat, les commerçants menacent de remobiliser
items.description: La tension reste vive au marché de Matoto. Après la manifestation organisée lundi par des vendeurs et vendeuses contre le marquage de leurs boutiques et magasins, Mohamed Soumah, l’un des manifestants, a été entendu ce mercredi 21 octobre 2026 au commissariat central de Matoto. En réaction, plusieurs commerçants se sont mobilisés sur place et menacent de reprendre la rue dès ce jeudi matin. À l’origine de la protestation, le marquage de plusieurs boutiques et magasins, accompagné d’une injonction de libérer les lieux dans un délai de 72 heures. Les commerçants concernés affirment ignorer l’identité des auteurs de cette opération. Ils indiquent également avoir sollicité des explications auprès du bureau du marché et de la mairie, sans obtenir de réponse claire sur les motifs de cette mesure. Estimant être visés par une opération de déguerpissement annoncée sans préavis formel, les vendeurs et vendeuses ont exprimé leur mécontentement à travers une manifestation dans l’enceinte du marché. Ce mercredi, l’affaire a connu un nouveau développement avec la plainte visant Mohamed Soumah en lien avec cette mobilisation. Selon ses déclarations à notre rédaction, des personnes se sont présentées à son domicile avant de le conduire au commissariat central de Matoto. « Ils ont porté plainte contre moi. Les gens sont venus chez moi pour me conduire au commissariat central de Matoto. C’est en rapport avec la manifestation du marché. Mais pour les détails, je n’ai aucune idée. Je dois me présenter là-bas. À l’heure où nous sommes, je suis en route pour là-bas », avait-il confié. Informés de sa présence au commissariat, plusieurs commerçants s’y sont rendus pour s’enquérir de sa situation. Sur place, des agents leur ont expliqué que leur camarade n’était pas en détention, mais qu’il était entendu au sujet des événements survenus lundi au marché. Après des échanges avec les forces de l’ordre, les commerçants ont finalement accepté de quitter les lieux pour retourner au marché et poursuivre leurs activités. Toutefois, le calme reste précaire. Les manifestants menacent d’organiser une nouvelle mobilisation dès ce jeudi matin et de barricader le passage si Mohamed Soumah n’est pas libéré dans la soirée de ce mercredi. Au moment de la mise en ligne de cet article, Mohamed Soumah se trouvait toujours dans les locaux du commissariat central de Matoto pour son audition. Selon des sources policières, il n’était pas en détention et n’avait pas été placé au violon. Mayi Cissé L’article Marché de Matoto : Mohamed Soumah entendu au commissariat, les commerçants menacent de remobiliser est apparu en premier sur Mediaguinee.com .
